outcome_notes: Price returned exactly to the entry level at the scheduled exit, meaning the HBM read-through and single-session rebound thesis produced zero directional follow-through — the catalysts (re-entry signal, packaging news) were either already priced in or insufficient to attract incremental buyers on the day. The small negative P&L despite a flat price move reflects costs absorbed for no thesis resolution.
risks_observed: Framing a 5-day pullback entry as a 'rebound day' play introduces mean-reversion logic into what is otherwise a momentum-oriented strategy, and the scheduled exit cap removed any ability to hold for multi-session thesis development. The prior flat/scheduled outcome on a similar MU setup was a visible pattern that should have flagged the recurring tendency toward non-directional behaviour as a position-sizing signal.

thesis: Q4 earnings tomorrow evening with concurrent PT raises from BofA ($240), Evercore ($245), and Guggenheim (high upside) creates a textbook pre-earnings drift window — RSI 54.9 leaves room to run, and the prior 0.00% flat outcome was a pure time-based exit without an imminent binary catalyst, making this setup structurally distinct.
outcome_notes: Pre-earnings drift materialised cleanly — the three concurrent PT raises provided a narrative anchor that sustained intraday buying, and the take-profit exit captured the drift window without exposing the position to overnight binary risk ahead of the Q4 print. Exiting intraday rather than holding to the close was the structurally correct decision given the earnings timing.
risks_observed: The strategy has no explicit guardrail preventing an overnight hold in a pre-earnings setup; had the take-profit not been hit, the position would have rolled into the binary event by default. If consensus estimate revisions had been pre-released or leaked, the drift window could have compressed abruptly — the thesis depended on the PT raises being the primary information event of the session, which held but is not guaranteed.

thesis: Silver is in historic collapse (-15.66% 20d, -9% 5d) driven by rising real rates (10Y at 4.55%) and firm dollar (DXY +1.99% 20d); this 3x short silver ETP has confirmed momentum with RSI 68.5, positive MACD, and volume 1.44x average — the macro regime is firmly supportive of further precious-metals downside, and this instrument was confirmed tradeable yesterday at adequate liquidity.
outcome_notes: VOIDED: yfinance returned a post-reverse-split LSE quote (~1822p) against a pre-split ledger entry (~15.65p) — no row in yfinance.splits to flag it. The recorded +11,895% was a units artefact, not a real intraday return. Voided to 0 P&L; the future-side guard in midday-TP and shadow EOD now refuses to book any |1-day return| > 80%.
risks_observed: An entry at $0.16 on a 3x leveraged ETP sits near a structural floor where bid-ask spread dominates and any intraday silver spike — on a Fed comment or safe-haven bid — could produce catastrophic drawdown before a stop fires. The position also carried implicit concentration risk: the overall basket was entirely precious-metals-short in character, leaving it fully exposed to a single correlated reversal.

thesis: The clearest legitimate uptrend in the candidate universe — volume 2.05x average confirms institutional participation behind 20d +14.77% momentum, with MACD positive and price above both SMAs; selected as the non-leveraged-short complement to 3SSI.L, diversifying away from the precious-metals data-integrity concerns affecting the rest of the field.
outcome_notes: Price was flat on the day and the scheduled exit captured nothing — the £-25 loss is purely transaction cost. The uptrend thesis neither confirmed nor failed intraday; the holding period was simply too short for any momentum to express itself.
risks_observed: Sized and positioned as a diversifier, WCCP.L provided no practical offset to the dominant leveraged-short exposure — the basket's risk was determined almost entirely by 3SSI.L. Using a scheduled (time-based) exit for a momentum leg means the strategy exits by the clock rather than by thesis invalidation, which structurally caps the upside that justified the entry.

thesis: Financials sector is Mildly Bullish in the macro framework (re-widening 3m/10y curve at 91bp expands NIM outlook), and Swiss legislative discussion of easing UBS capital requirements is a fresh, name-specific catalyst not yet fully reflected in price. 0.30% FX-only cost gate is low; predicted 1.0% intraday move clears the bar with margin.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere intraday and the scheduled exit recovered exactly entry — the capital-requirements catalyst produced zero same-session price discovery. The loss is pure transaction cost, confirming the thesis was real but multi-day in duration, not intraday.
risks_observed: Legislative catalysts are inherently unscheduled and asymmetric: positive news was speculative; any negative headline would have broken the trade hard. Thin intraday liquidity on UBSG.SW relative to EUR-listed European bank peers means spread and slippage absorbed the entire available edge before price moved at all.

thesis: Mid-cap semiconductor equipment (die-bonding for AI advanced packaging) aligns with today's brief theme of 'mid-cap AI/foundry plays repriced higher on server demand', offering rotation upside as capital flees mega-cap semis. Above both SMAs with above-average volume (1.18x) and 0.30% cost gate that a 0.9%+ intraday move clears cleanly.
outcome_notes: Price drove cleanly to the midday take-profit level with SMA alignment and above-average volume confirming participation; the AI/advanced-packaging rotation had genuine intraday momentum rather than just a thematic label. Exit was clean and the trigger behaved as designed.
risks_observed: Midday exit avoided the afternoon mean-reversion risk common in high-momentum mid-caps, but if the session continued higher the strategy systematically underparticipates in its best ideas. At the basket level, any concurrent semiconductor or AI-adjacent positions that day created correlated sector exposure — a single negative catalyst (e.g. a demand revision from a hyperscaler) would have hit multiple legs simultaneously.

thesis: 10-for-1 stock split effective June 12 is a confirmed, dated catalyst creating genuine pre-split retail demand for the remaining 2 sessions — high share price ($1,827) means affordability buying is a real driver post-split. Sector recovering from yesterday's oversold low with KLA specifically cited in the bounce, and cost gate clears easily at 0.30% round-trip.
outcome_notes: Price moved immediately against the position and hit the stop, suggesting the pre-split retail demand thesis either hadn't yet priced in or was overwhelmed by broader sector selling on the day. The split-anticipation edge proved insufficient to hold against intraday directional pressure with two sessions still remaining before the event.
risks_observed: Split-anticipation trades are notoriously front-run and can exhaust their bid before the event date — entering two sessions out left significant event-decay risk if the crowd had already positioned earlier in the week. No intraday catalyst existed to trigger fresh demand on entry day, making the stop exposure the dominant risk from the start.

thesis: Confirmed US-Iran clashes today reset Brent oil risk premium intraday — ENQ is a UK North Sea oil producer in an established uptrend (RSI 56, above both SMAs, +13.26% 20d) with elevated volume that will directly reprice higher on any oil spike. The catalyst is live and company-specific in impact.
outcome_notes: Oil risk premium repriced sharply on the geopolitical catalyst and ENQ tracked it cleanly, with the existing uptrend and elevated volume providing fuel for a quick 12% move before midday profit-taking captured the bulk of the intraday spike. Exit timing was well-judged — geopolitical oil spikes characteristically fade within the session once headlines stabilise.
risks_observed: A position sized to produce £220 gain on a £0.20 stock implies very high share count, meaning bid-ask spread and liquidity risk at exit were material — a worse fill on size could have compressed the return significantly. Correlation risk with other energy names in the basket was live; a single de-escalation headline would have hit all oil-linked positions simultaneously.

thesis: KOSPI AI chip rally (+16% in 48 hours driven by Samsung and SK Hynix) provides a fresh catalyst for this UK-listed Samsung ETF which sold off with US semis but remains above both SMAs; elevated volume (1.97×) today signals UK buyers already positioning into the Asian session recovery.
outcome_notes: The KOSPI rally failed to sustain into the UK session and SMSD sold off through the stop, indicating that European markets did not reprice the Asian chip recovery — likely because US semi sentiment remained a stronger anchor for the ETF than the Korean session gains. The elevated volume on entry may have reflected distribution rather than accumulation.
risks_observed: Cross-session ETF arbitrage theses carry structural lag risk: by London open the Asian move was already hours old and institutional desks had time to assess whether it was durable, so retail 'positioning into the recovery' was competing against informed sellers. This trade and KLA.DE both stopped out on the same day, suggesting the strategy had a directional bias toward risk-on that concentrated drawdown when the session turned.

thesis: CEO Meg O'Neill's disclosed strategic restructuring (dropping net zero division, splitting into upstream/downstream effective July) represents a material pivot toward higher oil leverage, while live Iran escalation risk repricing energy premium within today's session provides a fresh secondary catalyst. Transitional regime (VIX est. 18-28) — sizing reduced 30% from base; stop set below recent support to limit downside if the Iran bid reverses intraday.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere intraday — the scheduled exit closed the position flat against entry, with the £-15 loss entirely attributable to spread and commission. Neither the restructuring disclosure nor the Iran escalation premium produced a measurable directional move within the session window, suggesting both catalysts were already absorbed or failed to attract fresh institutional flow on the day.
risks_observed: Scheduled exits are a poor fit for disclosure catalysts that require institutional digestion over days rather than hours; the thesis had a structural time mismatch from the start. The dual-catalyst framing (corporate event + geopolitical repricing) created the appearance of confirmation but both drivers were correlated to the same underlying energy-sentiment bid, offering no real diversification of the entry rationale. In hindsight, no trailing stop or partial-exit ladder was in place to capture any intraday move had one occurred.

thesis: Healthcare is the uncontested macro leader (XLV #1 on both 5d and 20d timeframes), and HEAW.L is the only healthcare vehicle in the candidate set with tradeable volume (1.16x vs 0.02-0.04 for IHCU/XLVP/XSHC — those near-zero-volume ETFs explain the three consecutive zero returns, not the thesis). Meta-momentum is accelerating: 5d +3.56% is approximately 2× the implied daily rate from the 20d trend, MACD hist positive, RSI 60 is not extended, and both SMAs are supporting.
outcome_notes: Price was completely static from entry to scheduled exit — the healthcare momentum thesis had no time to express itself. The entire loss is cost-of-entry (spread and/or commissions), not adverse price action. Scheduled exit fired before any directional move developed.
risks_observed: A flat price through a scheduled exit suggests either the holding window is too short for a momentum thesis to resolve, or liquidity is thinner in practice than the 1.16x volume ratio implied at entry. No stop was in play, so if the exit had been delayed and price had reversed, downside was uncapped.

thesis: Highest volume ratio in the candidate universe (1.36x), backed by a clear macro tailwind — the yield curve steepened to 91bp (from 86.5bp last week), directly expanding NIM for domestic financials; the 5d pullback (-3.13%) within a strong 20d uptrend (+10.26%) creates a mean-reversion entry with RSI at a non-overbought 55 and no SMA violation.
outcome_notes: Same outcome as HEAW.L: entry and exit at identical price, loss attributable entirely to transaction costs. The yield-curve mean-reversion setup did not move in either direction during the holding period, making the scheduled exit a pure friction event.
risks_observed: Two consecutive flat-exit trades on the same day points to a holding-period mismatch — macro-driven NIM expansion plays on domestic financials typically resolve over days to weeks, not intraday or overnight. Both positions sharing a scheduled-exit mechanism with no profit target means every trade in this basket bleeds fees even when the thesis is directionally correct.

thesis: ETF structure removes single-name risk and 2.46× volume at RSI 14.5 confirms technical exhaustion rather than informed selling; the identical setup hit midday take-profit yesterday, validating buyer demand is present at these levels.
outcome_notes: The ETF bounced hard and fast, clearing midday take-profit with room to spare — the second consecutive session this exact setup resolved the same way, confirming active short-covering or rebalancing flows at that RSI level. Price action was directional from the open, not a slow grind, which is consistent with institutional re-entry rather than retail bottom-fishing.
risks_observed: Running the identical setup on the same instrument on back-to-back days compounds directional exposure: a macro reversal overnight would have turned two consecutive entries into two consecutive stops. The velocity of the intraday move also raises exit-slippage risk at the take-profit level, which the reported P&L may not fully reflect.

thesis: A 12.93× volume spike on a 13% 5-day decline with RSI 16.6 and no news catalyst is the strongest capitulation-exhaustion signal in today's pool — high participation on a moderate price fall indicates sellers have been absorbed, not that informed selling is ongoing.
outcome_notes: Selling resumed after entry and the stop triggered cleanly, disproving the absorption thesis. A volume multiple of 12.93× on a sub-£5 small-cap most likely reflected forced or institutional distribution into the oversold level, not exhaustion — the sheer size of that spike relative to the price decline was a distribution fingerprint, not a capitulation one.
risks_observed: Extreme volume multiples on micro-caps are a stronger warning flag than a confirming signal; thin analyst coverage means negative catalysts (covenant breaches, profit warnings) can circulate privately before appearing in screeners. The absence of a visible news catalyst is not the same as the absence of a catalyst.

thesis: 3.57× elevated volume with RSI 23.1 on a 38.6% 20-day drawdown signals active capitulation buying at the margin; the volume differentiates this from the near-zero-volume illiquid traps that failed this week.
outcome_notes: Price was completely flat over the hold and the scheduled exit recovered nothing — the volume differentiation from illiquid traps was correct in identifying active participation, but that participation was not sufficient to reverse a 38.6% structural slide within two days. The loss is again pure transaction cost.
risks_observed: A 3.57× volume multiple is relatively modest given the severity of the drawdown; the buying pressure identified was likely insufficient to absorb residual sell flow on a name this distressed. Sub-£4 UK small-caps with drawdowns of this magnitude carry material delisting and liquidity-gap risk that a 2-day mean-reversion window cannot price.

thesis: Broad-basket UK structure at RSI 18.4 with 1.26× volume on a 22% 20-day decline mirrors the LYXI.DE macro-flush reversal thesis with geographic diversification; ETF-like composition eliminates company-specific falling-knife risk.
outcome_notes: The UK mid-cap basket reversed cleanly from entry and hit midday take-profit alongside LYXI.DE, pointing to a shared macro risk-on flush across European equities rather than UK-specific demand. Price moved directionally from the session open with no material drawdown before the exit.
risks_observed: XMID.L and LYXI.DE hitting take-profit simultaneously exposes the basket-level correlation: the two positions were effectively a single macro-direction bet split across two instruments, with no hedge between them. A macro leg down on the same session would have stopped both out concurrently, concentrating the day's loss.

thesis: Healthcare ETF with the strongest MACD momentum signal in the candidate set (+2.832 histogram), fully aligned with the macro-bullish XLV thesis (W24 #1 sector on both timeframes); RSI at 63 and above both SMAs confirms the trend is healthy with room to extend today.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere from entry to exit — the MACD momentum signal produced no intraday follow-through and the scheduled exit resolved nothing about thesis validity. The entire loss is round-trip cost, meaning the signal was either stale by the time the position was opened or the day's session lacked a catalyst to extend the trend.
risks_observed: Running XLVP.L alongside HEAW.L in the same session doubled healthcare sector exposure with near-identical beta; a sector-level reversal would have hit both legs simultaneously. Two flat exits in the same sector on the same day is a hint that the momentum signal was already mean-reverting, not extending.

thesis: EU/UK financials ETF leading the non-healthcare group with +6.23% 5d and MACD strongly expanding, backed by the macro curve-steepening NIM tailwind (3m/10y at 91bp, widening); volume ratio 0.70 is the best in the non-tech universe, confirming genuine participation rather than stale price action.
outcome_notes: The 5-day trend and MACD expansion did not carry into intraday price action — exit matched entry exactly, and the position contributed nothing beyond friction costs. The scheduled exit means the financials thesis was never tested; the session simply closed without the curve-steepening narrative generating any observable bid.
risks_observed: A volume ratio of 0.70 — flagged as best-in-class but still well below neutral — should be treated as a liquidity warning rather than a participation signal; thin volume in a flat session can mask a tired move rather than confirm one. If rate expectations had shifted intraday, a thinly traded ETF would have widened spreads and amplified the exit cost.

thesis: Healthcare ETF distinguished from its low-volume peers by a volume ratio of 1.16 — the only healthcare name showing above-average buying activity today; MACD histogram expanding and RSI at 60.2 gives clean entry within the macro-bullish healthcare theme without doubling into an identical vehicle.
outcome_notes: Above-average volume ratio was the differentiating factor for entry, but buying activity did not translate into a net directional close — price was unchanged and the position exited on schedule. The volume signal may have reflected rebalancing or hedging flows rather than genuine directional conviction.
risks_observed: The basket held two healthcare ETFs (this and XLVP.L) with no offsetting short or uncorrelated position; concentration was effectively doubled at the sector level while appearing diversified by ticker. A hindsight signal: when all three basket names exit flat on a scheduled basis, the day's session had no edge for momentum strategies and the strategy should consider a regime filter before entering.

thesis: FDA approved EBGLYSS for every-8-week maintenance in atopic dermatitis today — the only option with 6 annual injections and no required topicals, a genuinely differentiated label that re-rates the franchise. Pharma is today's bullish sector and the reaction is fresh as of this morning's filing.
outcome_notes: Despite a genuinely differentiated FDA label and a bullish sector backdrop, price drifted lower through the session and exited at a loss on the scheduled close — a classic 'event already digested' dynamic where the approval had been partially anticipated by the options market or pre-positioned institutions who sold into the filing-day gap. No sustained follow-through buying materialised to extend the initial reaction.
risks_observed: At $1,151, LLY has a large absolute tick size that amplifies slippage and makes intraday noise costly relative to the basis-point P&L target; the scheduled-exit backstop rather than a trailing stop meant there was no mechanism to cut earlier if the thesis failed at the open. The FDA approval category of catalyst is also the most heavily pre-traded by pharma specialists, making day-of entry systematically late.

thesis: Applied Materials announced a $500M Singapore campus with 1,000 jobs specifically for AI infrastructure support today, signalling strong forward demand visibility from management. The stock has already outperformed SPY by +10% over 5 days and the expansion confirms the AI equipment cycle thesis ahead of next earnings.
outcome_notes: The capex announcement acted as a momentum accelerant rather than a standalone catalyst — the stock was already in a strong 5-day trend and management's forward-demand signal gave institutional buyers justification to add, pushing price to the take-profit target cleanly. The exit reason is consistent with the move being orderly rather than a spike-and-fade.
risks_observed: Entering a name already up 10% vs SPY over 5 days means the position absorbed maximum trend-following risk; a sector rotation out of semis or a broader AI-sentiment reversal intraday would have hit an extended entry with no cushion. AMAT, LRCX, and KLAC tend to move together, so any concurrent semi-equipment position in the book would have created unintended sector concentration on the same AI-capex factor.

thesis: Confirmed US retaliatory strikes against Iran with an explicit 72-hour escalation window directly reprices Lockheed's missile, air-defence, and strike-aircraft product lines. Defence stocks are explicitly on watch and the catalyst is geopolitical, not just sentiment — lower conviction due to weak technical structure (below both MAs) so sized accordingly.
outcome_notes: The geopolitical catalyst failed to deliver incremental repricing during the session — LMT barely moved, suggesting the Iran-strike premium had already been absorbed into defence names before entry or that broader risk-off sentiment offset the sector tailwind. The weak technical structure flagged at entry proved predictive: below both MAs, the stock had no trend momentum to amplify the news.
risks_observed: Geopolitical catalysts are the hardest to time because the market's first move often overshoots, and subsequent sessions can mean-revert if no new escalation arrives within the 72-hour window — the scheduled exit enforced a fixed hold rather than allowing flexibility to cut if the escalation narrative went quiet. At the basket level, holding both LLY and LMT on the same day — one a sector-momentum play, one a geopolitical hedge — provided superficial diversification while both shared the same 'news-driven same-session fade' failure mode.

thesis: Health Care is the strategy's top macro-aligned sector (XLV Bullish, +3.25% 5d, +6.38% 20d) and UNH is a core defensive expression in today's risk-off tape driven by Iran escalation; above both SMAs with no company-specific negatives, providing the clearest alignment between macro thesis and technical setup.
outcome_notes: Price sold off steadily from entry and hit the stop; UNH declined rather than acting as a flight-to-safety destination in the risk-off tape. The move looks company-specific — above-SMA technicals provided no resistance against what appears to be idiosyncratic selling pressure.
risks_observed: Running two Health Care names simultaneously meant the sector bet was effectively doubled; when UNH stopped out it called into question the XLV thesis rather than just the individual name, leaving LLY's flat position looking like residual exposure with no offset. UNH carries material headline risk that above-SMA screening does not filter — the 'no company-specific negatives' check needs a harder look at litigation and regulatory overhang.

thesis: Applied Materials has two today-specific positive catalysts — Cantor Fitzgerald raising the PT to $650 and a $500M Singapore manufacturing expansion — that distinguish it from the broader mega-cap semi selloff; strong technicals (RSI 62.7, above SMA20 at $449 and SMA50 at $412) confirm the semi-equipment cycle is tracking independently of AI inference names.
outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly from entry to the midday take-profit target, with the name separating from broader semi weakness throughout the session. The catalyst-driven bid was the dominant intraday force and the exit captured the move before any mean-reversion risk built.
risks_observed: Exiting at midday was conservative — if the PT raise and capacity news sustained buying into the close, meaningful upside was forfeited. More broadly, holding a single semi-equipment name with no correlated hedge left the position fully exposed to any shift in macro sentiment that could have dragged AMAT back toward the sector despite the company-specific tailwinds.

thesis: Health Care is the top-ranked macro sector (bullish, +3.25% 5d, +6.38% 20d) and today's fresh FDA approval for EBGLYSS every-8-week dosing in atopic dermatitis is a new catalyst distinct from yesterday's TRIUMPH-1 flow, providing intraday buying momentum on top of an already-clean technical setup above both SMAs with RSI not yet overbought.
outcome_notes: The dosing-frequency approval drove clean intraday buying that carried price straight to the take_profit level with no meaningful reversal attempt. Technical structure held as expected — the above-SMA base absorbed the catalyst without the chop that typically accompanies news-driven moves into resistance. Exit reason matched intent; no slippage or early exit pressure.
risks_observed: Running LLY alongside ABBV on the same session doubled Health Care sector concentration, so any sector-level reversal (e.g. surprise drug-pricing headline) would have compressed both simultaneously. The FDA catalyst was publicly available pre-market, making a 'sell the news' fade a live risk that didn't materialise but warranted a tighter initial stop than a pure technical setup would require.

thesis: AbbVie sits squarely in the macro-bullish Health Care sector and today has two near-term catalysts — a CNBC Final Trades buy recommendation and whale-alert institutional flow — while RSI at 61.9 and a building MACD histogram signal room to run without overbought risk.
outcome_notes: Neither the CNBC mention nor the institutional flow alert produced any measurable intraday price movement — the scheduled exit captured exactly the entry price. The catalysts appear to have been fully absorbed before the session or failed to attract incremental buyers during the holding window.
risks_observed: The scheduled exit mechanism provided no price-based protection: the position sat idle through a zero-movement session with the only loss being cost/FX drag, meaning a reversal of equivalent magnitude would not have been cut. Paired with LLY, the dual Health Care exposure on a single macro thesis meant idiosyncratic disappointment in one name had no offset from sector diversification.

thesis: Goldman sits in the mildly-bullish Financials sector and benefits directly from the 3m/10y curve widening to 91bp (expanding NIM) and a stronger dollar that is neutral-to-positive for domestic capital markets revenues; a soft CPI print today would add to the tailwind while the 5d lag (-0.34%) means the move has not yet been front-run.
outcome_notes: The curve-widening and dollar-strength setup did not translate into any intraday price action within the holding window — price was flat at the scheduled exit. The 'catch-up lag' framing required a multi-day timeframe to play out, which was mismatched against a same-session exit structure.
risks_observed: The thesis carried a soft-CPI conditional that introduced binary macro event risk; if CPI came in hot the tailwind inverted, but no stop was structured around that outcome. The scheduled exit rather than a stop or momentum-based exit meant there was no mechanism to cut the position if the macro backdrop shifted intraday, leaving the cost drag as the only realised loss by chance rather than by design.

thesis: S&P 500 inclusion confirmed June 9 — same mechanical catalyst as our MRVL +13.5% trade, but FLEX has not yet reacted (5-day return of +1.91% predates the announcement, today is effectively day 1 of trading the news). Mandatory passive rebalancing buying is macro-agnostic and will execute regardless of broader tech selloff. Transitional regime (hot CPI + Iran = estimated VIX 22–28) applied as 30% size reduction; predicted +4.5% over 2 days clears the 2× variant threshold of 3.6% for a name without a strict 8-K anchor.
outcome_notes: The passive rebalancing demand failed to materialise within the trade window — price sold off continuously from entry to stop rather than absorbing index-inclusion buying. The risk-off session (hot CPI, geopolitical) overwhelmed mechanical flows, suggesting either the inclusion was front-run before entry or the effective rebalancing date was further out than day 1.
risks_observed: Index-inclusion trades without an 8-K anchor carry significant timing risk: if faster participants front-run the announcement, the position enters into exhausted demand rather than ahead of it. The 30% size reduction for transitional regime was correct directionally but structural — it couldn't protect against a scenario where the entire thesis was timing-dependent and the window had already closed.

thesis: Primary-grade 8-K anchor (Item 8.01, June 8) confirms $1.25B definitive cash acquisition of Vega Therapeutics' rare bleeding disorder asset — no dilution risk. HC Wainwright PT raise to $140 (+39% from $100.64) published June 9 confirms analyst re-rating is still in progress; volume 1.84x average and RSI 57 (room to run) support day-2 continuation. Pharma sector is bullish-leaning per today's news brief; transitional regime sizing applied.
outcome_notes: The HC Wainwright PT raise to $140 (pre-market June 10) acted as a discrete second-day catalyst on top of the acquisition anchor, driving price well beyond the 3% TP trigger and into the $106.87 midday exit — a level the stock subsequently faded from, with the daily close returning only ~+2%. The midday sweep exit fortuitously caught near the intraday peak, validating the day-2 continuation thesis while also revealing that the analyst re-rating energy was largely exhausted by midday.
risks_observed: Running the same single-name biotech catalyst into a second session concentrates binary deal-risk — any adverse 8-K amendment or financing noise would have gapped the position with no warning across both days of exposure. The midday sweep exit mechanism introduces meaningful exit-timing variance: the +6.19% capture was lucky relative to the close; a later intraday peak would have produced a significantly worse result with identical trade logic.

thesis: Applied Materials' +6.5% EPS beat from May 14 is generating active drift: +13% over 20 days, +7.4% over the last 5 days, RSI 62.7 with both SMAs below price. Today's $500M Singapore manufacturing expansion and Cantor's PT raise to $650 reinforce the narrative. At ~19 trading days post-print, 5 more sessions keeps us within the optimal drift window.
outcome_notes: Active drift continued through the session and the midday take-profit trigger fired into strength, with the Singapore capex announcement and Cantor PT raise providing fresh institutional attention that accelerated the move. The thesis held cleanly: drift was already in motion and the news-flow reinforced rather than initiated it.
risks_observed: The exit at $529 against a freshly raised $650 PT suggests the midday rule cut off a trade that still had fundamental runway — useful to flag for calibrating the take-profit threshold when a same-day catalyst materially changes the upside case. AMAT carrying the day while both software legs stopped out also highlights how thin the basket-level diversification was: one winner absorbed two losers, making the net result more path-dependent than the individual setups implied.

thesis: Eli Lilly's +16.9% EPS beat has sustained clean drift (+21.2% over 20 days); today's FDA approval for EBGLYSS every-8-week maintenance dosing is an incremental positive catalyst on top of established momentum. RSI 69.8 in confirmed trend, well above both SMAs. 3-day hold captures near-term FDA reaction while managing late-stage drift risk at elevated RSI.
outcome_notes: Day-1 drift came through cleanly (+2.53% on June 11), validating the PEAD continuation. The scheduled exit on June 12 captured $1168.53 near the open before an intraday reversal that ultimately closed the stock down ~2.5% on the day — timing of the fixed 3-day exit worked in the trade's favour here rather than by design.
risks_observed: RSI had climbed to ~71 by exit day and the reversal materialised as flagged by same-day models, meaning a later or EOD exit would have surrendered most of the gain. The 25% single-name allocation in a pharma name with an active GLP-1 competitive overhang (AstraZeneca Phase 3) represents meaningful concentration risk that a news-reactive filter did flag but the PEAD system has no mechanism to act on.

thesis: Tenable's +113.1% EPS beat generated strong 20-day drift (+26.25%), and the recent 5-day pullback (-6%) is occurring above both SMAs (RSI 61.1), consistent with healthy consolidation in an uptrend rather than drift reversal. May 21 Investor Day reaffirmed management confidence. Sized smaller to reflect uncertainty about beat quality composition and late-stage drift timing.
outcome_notes: Price recovered cleanly from the pre-entry pullback and reached the midday take-profit level, confirming the consolidation-within-uptrend read. The drift continued to resolve in the expected direction with no intraday reversal that would have suggested exhaustion. Exit was mechanical and timely — no sign the position needed to be held longer.
risks_observed: At 20+ days post-earnings, drift premium is largely harvested; holding past the take-profit for incremental gain would have carried asymmetric downside. Beat quality (EPS composition uncertainty flagged at entry) was never resolved — a revenue-miss-masked-by-cost-cuts scenario could have unravelled quickly on any follow-on news. Single-name basket today means no cross-position cushion; a sector-level cybersecurity risk-off move would have had no offset.

thesis: Partners Group at RSI 23.1 with a 5-day stabilization (+2.85%) and sector-positive private credit commentary — quality asset manager at a technically extreme oversold reading with no fundamental negative catalyst. FX-only costs (0.30% round-trip) give comfortable margin over the 2-day gate threshold of 0.90%.
outcome_notes: The oversold reading did not produce a snap-back within the holding window — price drifted a further 2.4% lower and the scheduled exit captured the full drawdown. The 5-day stabilisation turned out to be a consolidation before continuation rather than a base, suggesting the private credit repricing was still in progress at entry.
risks_observed: CHF/GBP FX exposure added unhedged currency risk on a name already moving against the thesis; the 'no fundamental negative catalyst' assumption is fragile for an illiquid Swiss-listed alternative asset manager where sentiment shifts can be slow-moving and hard to detect intraday. The scheduled exit as the only backstop meant there was no mechanism to cut the trade once the reversion window had clearly passed.

thesis: RSI 19.4 with above-average volume (1.35×) on a 5-day decline of 11% in the absence of any identified negative news — the volume pattern is consistent with capitulation rather than distribution. Predicted 1.8% return clears the 1-day cost gate of 1.05% (FX + French FTT) with a 0.75% buffer; extending to 2-day would breach the gate.
outcome_notes: Price recovered cleanly to the take-profit level within the 1-day window, confirming the capitulation read on the volume/RSI confluence. The swift exit suggests the reversal was sharp rather than a slow grind, which is consistent with a flush-and-recover pattern rather than a sustained bid returning.
risks_observed: The French FTT makes this market structurally punishing for any trade that stalls — a 1-day delay to exit would have consumed the buffer entirely, turning a marginal winner into a loser. The absence of confirmed news context cuts both ways: capitulation was the right read here, but an undiscovered negative catalyst (earnings leak, index deletion) would have looked identical on entry.

thesis: RSI 9.4 is one of the most extreme oversold readings in the candidate list for a stock with a real price, and the 5-day decline of -5% is moderating relative to the 20-day trend — FX-only costs (0.30%) provide generous cost-gate clearance. Position sized small given lack of news context on the decline catalyst.
outcome_notes: RSI 9.4 proved a reliable exhaustion signal; price moved to take-profit without apparent struggle, suggesting the selling pressure had genuinely dissipated rather than pausing. The moderating 5-day vs. 20-day slope was the key discriminator — it indicated the move was decelerating, not accelerating.
risks_observed: At €1.12, bid-ask spread and exchange fees represent a disproportionately large share of the expected gain relative to a higher-priced name — any adverse fill quality would erode the edge materially. The unknown decline catalyst is the most significant residual risk: with both this and EXE.PA hitting take-profit on the same session, a basket-wide market tailwind may have carried trades that had weaker idiosyncratic setups, flattering the strategy's signal quality on this date.

thesis: Financials is the macro-aligned sector of choice on a risk-off higher-for-longer day, with the steepening yield curve (91bp) expanding NIM for domestic banks; Swiss lawmakers actively weighing capital relief for UBS is a same-session re-rating catalyst that gives this pick a clear stock-level edge above the sector thesis.
outcome_notes: Price drifted below entry without a meaningful bid and triggered the stop, indicating the capital-relief catalyst either failed to land intraday or was already priced. The broader NIM expansion thesis may have been macro-valid, but UBSG specifically couldn't hold the entry level — the stock-specific edge didn't materialise within the session window.
risks_observed: Regulatory catalysts carry headline-timing risk: if the Swiss legislative development didn't hit newswires during active hours, the position reduced to plain sector exposure with a tight stop. In hindsight, sizing a legislative catalyst on a single name inside a risk-off session left almost no buffer for the normal intraday volatility that financials exhibit before a re-rating actually prints.

thesis: Energy is today's macro-bullish sector with US-Iran escalation and crude inventory declines providing dual supply tailwinds; Naturgy's natural gas infrastructure exposure above both SMAs with confirming volume (1.11) makes it the cleanest European expression of the energy bid without the direct spot-oil volatility.
outcome_notes: NTGY sold off through entry and stopped out despite the macro supply narrative, suggesting European nat-gas infrastructure decoupled from the crude-driven energy bid on the day — possibly on gas storage or EU regulatory overhang. The volume confirmation at entry didn't translate into directional follow-through, which often signals the move had already exhausted itself before the session open.
risks_observed: The trade conflated crude oil supply dynamics with European piped-gas infrastructure, two exposures that can diverge sharply within a single session; the macro catalyst (US-Iran, crude inventories) had no direct transmission mechanism to NTGY's revenue base. Combined with UBSG stopping out simultaneously, the basket was briefly running two losing positions against each other with no offsetting leg — a basket-level correlation risk that wasn't visible in the individual setups.

thesis: Consumer Staples is the textbook rotation destination on a risk-off CPI-surprise day as higher-for-longer reprices growth sectors lower; ULVR's +5.63% 5d momentum, above-SMA positioning, and improving MACD histogram make it the best technical expression of that defensive rotation in the UK market.
outcome_notes: The position went nowhere and exited flat at the scheduled time — no drawdown, but also no rotation bid materialised in price despite the risk-off macro read. The technical setup was intact (held above SMAs), but the anticipated inflows to defensives either hadn't arrived by session end or were offset by broader FTSE selling pressure.
risks_observed: A flat exit on a momentum-led thesis is a signal that the +5.63% 5d run may have pre-empted the rotation rather than preceded it — late entry into an already-expressed defensive move. At the basket level, all three positions on this day closed at zero or negative, which points to a systematic issue: either the macro regime call was correct but the session-level timing was off, or the individual name selection consistently lagged the actual flows. That pattern is worth auditing across prior macro-aligned sessions.

thesis: Health Care is the sole Bullish-rated macro sector and Alcon is its clearest technical expression — outperforming SPY by +7.37% over 5 days with MACD histogram turning positive from a neutral RSI base; under a transitional regime, concentrating in the highest-conviction macro-sector alignment is the primary risk control, and the ongoing risk-off rotation from CPI/higher-for-longer provides today's session catalyst.
outcome_notes: Price drifted ~0.46 points against entry through the session and closed red, with the scheduled exit capturing the full drawdown rather than a stop. The risk-off / higher-for-longer catalyst that was supposed to be the session driver either didn't arrive in a form that benefited defensives intraday or was offset by broader CHF-denominated selling pressure. The MACD histogram uptick confirmed a prior inflection but did not translate into intraday follow-through.
risks_observed: ALC.SW and NOVN.SW are both CHF-denominated Swiss HC names held simultaneously, concentrating currency risk and single-country exposure within the same macro-sector basket. ALC's 5-day outperformance of +7.37% vs SPY may have already priced in the macro tailwind, leaving limited room for a catalyst to add alpha on entry day.

thesis: Partners Group sits in the Mildly Bullish Financials sector and is flashing a rare RSI 23.1 floor signal with the +2.85% 5d bounce already underway (+5.40% vs SPY); the Arcmont CEO confirming private credit default rates remain low removes the key fundamental bear-case, and the 0.30% round-trip cost gate means even a modest continuation of the oversold bounce clears the bar with margin.
outcome_notes: The scheduled exit triggered with zero net price movement, meaning the oversold bounce did not continue within the holding window — the RSI floor signal identified the trough but failed to generate follow-through momentum before the time limit. Cost drag was the sole detractor, confirming the round-trip cost gate was not cleared.
risks_observed: Time-bounded entries on bounce signals are structurally vulnerable when the catalyst (here, the Arcmont credit commentary) is already priced in at entry — the 5d move had done the work before the position was opened. The CHF-to-GBP translation adds a silent drag on flat-price exits that the cost gate modelling should account for explicitly; the nominal loss on a 0.00% price return likely reflects this FX haircut.

thesis: Shell's Merlin-1X light oil discovery offshore Namibia (disclosed June 10) is a primary corporate exploration disclosure the market has not yet priced in — stock is flat on the week despite the announcement (RSI 51). Trump's imminent-Iran-strike threats add fresh macro tailwind via oil premium, and Shell's CEO is publicly bullish on multi-year oil demand. Predicted +2.0% comfortably clears the 1.5% stamp-duty cost gate; transitional regime (est. VIX 20–25) warrants the 30%-discounted 20% allocation.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere from entry to the scheduled exit, generating a flat price return that turned negative after transaction costs. The Merlin-1X catalyst had already been absorbed — the thesis itself flagged the stock was flat on the week post-announcement, which was a sign the market had already discounted the news rather than a signal of delayed repricing. No macro oil premium from the Iran narrative appeared within the holding window.
risks_observed: The thesis contained its own red flag: citing a flat post-announcement price as evidence of mispricing rather than as evidence the catalyst was spent. Stamp duty makes a flat exit a guaranteed loser on UK equities, so any trade where the catalyst may already be priced needs a higher conviction signal than RSI 51. Scheduled exit left no room for asymmetric recovery if the move was merely delayed.

thesis: Healthcare is the top-ranked sector on both 5d (+4.87%) and 20d (+7.02%) timeframes, fully macro-aligned with the defensive rotation away from real-rate-sensitive growth sectors. IHCU.L has the cleanest setup — above both SMAs, RSI 65 with room to run, MACD expanding, and 0.92x volume confirming normal participation rather than the rebalancing noise seen in HEAW.L.
outcome_notes: Price was unchanged from entry to exit — the healthcare momentum thesis generated no intraday price appreciation within the holding window. The scheduled exit fired without any directional move materialising; the £20 loss is entirely transaction friction (spread and/or commission), not adverse price action. Sector tailwinds may have been backward-looking by the time of entry.
risks_observed: A fixed scheduled exit with no trailing stop or price target means a momentum thesis has no mechanism to run beyond the scheduled window or cut short a deteriorating position. With both legs of the basket closing flat on the same session, the strategy is structurally exposed to days where macro alignment exists but intraday catalysts do not — in those sessions the only certain outcome is cost bleed.

thesis: Financials is the top non-defensive sector with curve steepening to 91bp supporting NIM expansion; XUFB.L is above both SMAs, MACD positive and expanding, volume 1.07x confirms genuine participation. Provides sector diversification away from the healthcare-only exposure that produced doubled beta in recent sessions.
outcome_notes: Identical outcome to the IHCU.L leg — flat price, scheduled exit, loss is cost-only. The curve steepening thesis (91bp spread supporting NIM expansion) is a multi-session or multi-week driver; it produced no same-session price response in XUFB.L.
risks_observed: The diversification rationale (reducing healthcare-only beta) was not tested — both positions behaved identically, so basket-level correlation was 1.0 on the day regardless of sector difference. Holding a cyclical financials leg alongside a defensive healthcare leg into a scheduled exit also means the two positions can work against each other on any session with a clear risk-on/risk-off tilt, with no stop on either side to limit the losing leg.

thesis: Health Care is the #1 ranked sector on both 5-day (+5.58%) and 20-day (+8.06%) relative strength with an explicit Bullish macro rating; XLVP.L carries the strongest MACD histogram (+2.785) among all healthcare candidates, confirming accelerating momentum above both SMAs — meta-momentum composite ranks highest as XLV transitions from mid-pack to cycle leader, and domestic revenue mix is immune to the dollar headwind hitting tech and materials.
outcome_notes: Price was unchanged from entry to the scheduled exit, so the momentum thesis produced no intraday directionality within the holding window. The -£20 result is purely frictional — the sector-level signal may have been valid but the realisation horizon was shorter than the timeframe the 5-/20-day strength reading requires.
risks_observed: A time-capped exit with zero price movement flags a mismatch between the signal's lookback window and the trade's holding period — strong multi-week relative strength doesn't guarantee same-session follow-through. Running this alongside XUFB.L also concentrated the basket in two rate-sensitive, macro-defensive sectors simultaneously, leaving the portfolio exposed to any single macro reversal (e.g., a surprise yield move or risk-off flush).

thesis: Financials upgraded to Mildly Bullish on yield-curve steepening to 91bp (re-expanding NIM) with dollar strength neutral-to-positive for domestic banks; XUFB.L leads the full candidate universe in 20-day return (+8.77%), sits above both SMAs with healthy volume (1.07×), and provides sector diversification against the concentrated healthcare position — meta-momentum score improving as financials rank has risen from ~4th to consistently top-4 over the past 4 weeks.
outcome_notes: Exited at entry price on the scheduled trigger — the yield-curve steepening/NIM thesis had no opportunity to express itself within the holding window. Zero price capture means the 20-day momentum rank correctly identified relative strength historically but offered no edge on the specific session held.
risks_observed: The diversification rationale (offsetting the concentrated healthcare position) was undercut by both legs exiting flat on the same schedule, suggesting the basket sizing and exit logic aren't calibrated to each other. The financials thesis is also conditionally dependent on the yield curve continuing to steepen — any intraday flattening would have invalidated the core driver before the position had time to move.

thesis: Healthcare USD is the undisputed #1 sector on both 5d (+4.87%) and 20d (+7.02%) timeframes with a clean RSI 65 and above both SMAs; the macro regime — rising real rates, strong dollar — systematically bids defensives, and this is the most liquid healthcare name in the candidate set (volume ratio 0.92x). Predicted 1.8% clears the 1-day cost gate of 1.25%.
outcome_notes: Price was completely unchanged at the scheduled exit — exit matched entry to the cent, so the 5d sector leadership signal produced zero intraday continuation. The -£12 loss is entirely stamp duty paid at entry, confirming the 1-day holding window offered no catalyst beyond what was already priced in at the open.
risks_observed: Stamp duty creates a fixed ~0.5% structural headwind that the cost gate calculation (1.25%) did not fully account for — actual break-even was tighter than the gate implied. Both basket legs going flat simultaneously points to a USD defensive flow pause at the session level, not noise in either name individually; a basket-correlation filter would have flagged this as elevated co-movement risk before entry.

thesis: Consumer Staples USD provides a second defensive-rotation long with a different underlying driver (stable demand + USD-hedged exposure) than healthcare; RSI 55 leaves room versus IHCU.L's 65, volume ratio 0.85x is the second-best in the candidate set, and the 5.23% 5d return confirms the macro rotation is already in motion. Predicted 1.4% clears the 1-day gate of 1.25%.
outcome_notes: Identical outcome to IHCU.L — price closed at the exact open level with no directional movement across the session. The 5.23% 5d momentum had already consolidated by the entry date; without a fresh intraday driver the predicted 1.4% move had no mechanism to materialise within one day.
risks_observed: Of the two positions, this had the narrowest predicted-vs-gate margin (1.4% vs 1.25%), making it the most sensitive to any execution slippage or stamp duty drag — there was essentially no room for a partial win. Running it alongside IHCU.L concentrated the basket in two correlated USD-denominated defensive ETFs on the same exchange, meaning a single regime event (dollar stall, LSE liquidity thin) would hit both simultaneously, as it did here.

thesis: FDA approved EBGLYSS every-8-week maintenance dosing (June 10) — the only atopic dermatitis biologic with six annual injections and no required topicals — a differentiated label expansion that extends the commercial moat. Catalyst is one session old with below-average volume suggesting institutional accumulation is still building rather than finished.
outcome_notes: Price was unchanged at the scheduled exit, implying the market either fully priced the EBGLYSS dosing expansion before entry or found an offsetting headwind (sector rotation, broad pharma weakness) that neutralised the catalyst. The anticipated second-wave institutional accumulation did not show up in price action.
risks_observed: Entering a one-session-old FDA catalyst in large-cap pharma is structurally late — information is rapidly distributed and buy-side participants reprice efficiently, leaving little asymmetry for day-2 entries. The £-6.77 cost drag on a zero-price-move outcome highlights that break-even at the position level required actual follow-through, not just a held bid.

thesis: Today's TARGAN acquisition (June 11) confirms M&A execution against the CEO's stated $1-15B strategy, with the May 22 8-K debt offering signalling the war chest was raised specifically for this deployment; ISLEND HIV Phase 3 success de-risked the franchise and RSI 54.3 leaves room to absorb continued positive news flow in a risk-off session that favours defensive pharma.
outcome_notes: No price movement by scheduled exit — the TARGAN announcement and pipeline de-risking narrative produced zero observable lift, and the defensive-pharma risk-off bid anticipated in the thesis did not materialise either. The catalyst stack was real but apparently discounted ahead of entry.
risks_observed: Running LLY and MRK simultaneously in the same session created correlated pharma exposure: both went flat, and any sector-level headwind (drug pricing headlines, macro rotation away from defensives) would have hit both simultaneously with no offset. The basket on this day had meaningful concentration in large-cap pharma catalyst trades, amplifying the effect of any sector-wide repricing that muted individual news.

thesis: Health Care is the top macro sector (Bullish W24 rating, XLV +3.59% 5d) and today's risk-off CPI print reinforces defensive rotation into quality names. JNJ's IMAAVY approval for wAIHA — a disease with zero FDA-approved therapies — is a true new-market catalyst, not a label extension, providing a fresh intraday flow driver above and beyond the ongoing IOL expansion.
outcome_notes: Price was unchanged from entry to scheduled exit — the IMAAVY approval and defensive-rotation tailwinds generated no intraday follow-through, suggesting the catalyst was either priced in pre-open or overwhelmed by broad market indifference. The £-6.77 loss is purely transactional (spread/FX), not directional. Exit was passive rather than thesis-driven.
risks_observed: Back-to-back flat exits on HC names (JNJ today, ABBV yesterday and today) indicate that event-driven catalysts in this sector are being digested before the open, leaving intraday entries with little edge. Running JNJ and ABBV simultaneously doubled HC concentration while both positions contributed zero price gain, amplifying opportunity cost relative to the semi names.

thesis: Health Care macro Bullish with ABBV in a clean technical uptrend (above SMA20 and SMA50, RSI 64.6, MACD positive). A fresh CNBC final trade pick today with an 'expanded label' thesis provides an event-driven catalyst distinct from yesterday's general bullishness that produced a flat exit, giving this a cleaner entry point for intraday follow-through.
outcome_notes: Second consecutive flat exit on this ticker — the CNBC catalyst and re-entry framing added no incremental intraday movement. Price held the technical structure but showed no catalyst-driven buying interest during the session, and the scheduled exit confirmed the thesis simply didn't activate.
risks_observed: Repeating a trade that already produced a flat exit the prior day is a red flag the signal is stale — the 'fresh entry point' argument didn't overcome an already-absorbed catalyst. Combined with JNJ, the two HC positions consumed roughly equal capital to the two winning semis while delivering zero directional return, revealing a structural basket imbalance where all gains came from a single thematic cluster.

thesis: Semiconductor equipment is structurally insulated from single-session risk-off selling — tool orders are contracted capex, not spot demand. Two independent analyst upgrades today (UBS to $570, Cantor to $650) alongside a $500M Singapore expansion announcement confirm institutional conviction; a 2-day hold allows upgrade-driven institutional accumulation to build above today's noise.

AI data-center interconnect demand is resilient even in a risk-off tech session; CRDO's +5.46% 5d and +14.88% 20d with price above both SMAs shows it is one of the few tech names genuinely holding its trend. Tom Lee's GRNJ ETF rebalance adding CRDO confirms fresh institutional recognition; 2-day hold allows the momentum structure to extend before the broader tech headwind reasserts.
outcome_notes: Momentum extended cleanly through midday, with AI-interconnect demand holding up in a risk-off tape and ETF rebalance flow providing an identifiable incremental buyer. The take-profit fired at +7.63% — the strongest single-name return in the basket — and price action showed no premature exhaustion before the trigger.
risks_observed: CRDO is a high-beta name where a delayed or smaller-than-expected ETF rebalance, or a sharp intraday tech rotation, could have reversed a 7% move before the take-profit fired. At the basket level, the day's outcome was binary: two semis carried everything, two HC names gave nothing — a concentration pattern that worked today but represents a structural fragility in the strategy's sector diversification.

thesis: RSI at 11.9 and −32% over five sessions on near-normal volume (1.10×) with no visible fundamental negative news — a classic REIT technical oversell. Previous trade was flat rather than a loss and entered at a materially higher level; the setup is now more extreme, targeting partial intraday reversion toward $3.10–3.15 with a tight 10% stop given mean-reversion asymmetric downside risk.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere intraday — the scheduled exit triggered at the same level as entry, indicating zero mean-reversion progress within the trade window. The extreme RSI reading was real but the catalyst for intraday snap-back never materialised; the £-4.86 loss on a flat price move is attributable to spread/FX friction rather than adverse direction.
risks_observed: A -32% multi-session decline in a REIT at this price level ($2.90) raises the possibility of structural selling — rate sensitivity, credit concerns, or forced liquidation — that technical oversell signals cannot distinguish from random noise. Time-boxed exits on non-directional days consume capital without stop protection doing any work; if the setup re-queues at the same level, the prior flat trade is now two consecutive non-events on the same name.

thesis: Reconciled from Alpaca portfolio (slot 1) — original ledger entry missing (likely an entry-run timeout or smart-merge race). Daily exit will close this normally.
outcome_notes: C delivered +2.75% on the day, consistent with the multi-catalyst setup documented in the same-day prediction: a $17.5B Amazon credit facility mandated to Citibank, a CFO Q2 trading-revenue upgrade, and Citi's notable absence from the DOJ debanking probe that weighed on peers. Price moved cleanly in one direction with no intraday reversal to the close; the scheduled exit captured effectively the full day's range. Direction was right even if the prediction's strong_up label slightly overstated the eventual move.
risks_observed: Neither stop-loss nor take-profit was set on this position (both null) — a consequence of the reconciled entry bypassing normal thesis-logging and parameter injection. Had any of the three catalysts reversed intraday (e.g., probe news expanding to Citi), there was no mechanical floor. The reconciliation path itself is a structural risk: entries that survive the session without a ledger record accumulate without the usual pre-trade safety checks.

thesis: Reconciled from Alpaca portfolio (slot 1) — original ledger entry missing (likely an entry-run timeout or smart-merge race). Daily exit will close this normally.
outcome_notes: INCY extended its Vega Therapeutics M&A re-rating into a third consecutive up-day, gaining +2.72% against a 1.5% prediction — the HC Wainwright PT raise to $140 and sustained above-average volume both held as valid continuation signals. The actual exit outperformed the prediction materially, suggesting day-3 institutional accumulation was stronger than the conviction-0.65 estimate implied. Scheduled exit caught the full move; there was no sign of momentum exhaustion by close.
risks_observed: Day-3 M&A momentum is inherently fragile: any deal-risk headline (regulatory, financing, target pushback) could have reversed the move sharply, and with stop_loss_pct null there was no backstop. Both positions in today's basket were reconciled entries with missing safety parameters, so the basket had zero mechanical risk controls on a day where a sector-wide risk-off event (or acquisition collapses) would have hit both simultaneously.

thesis: Frasers Group (Mike Ashley) launched a €2.67bn bid for full Hugo Boss ownership on June 11 — volume spiked to 5.49× average as merger arb desks step in, and the market is pricing a revised higher offer given Ashley's track record of increasing bids. With the stock still trading below a full premium valuation, today's session should see continued drift toward fair-value M&A pricing.
outcome_notes: Price was completely flat across the holding period — no continued drift toward bid-premium fair value occurred. The scheduled exit confirms the market had already absorbed the Frasers announcement at the prior session's close, with no incremental arb buying to push the spread tighter during this session.
risks_observed: Entering a merger-arb name after a high-volume spike day means the easy premium expansion has typically already occurred; spread compression risk is asymmetric if no formal offer documentation follows promptly. FX drag (EUR/GBP) consumed the entire P&L on a flat price, a structural cost that arb trades with small expected moves cannot easily absorb.

thesis: Novartis's del-brax (acquired via the $12B Avidity deal) met its primary endpoint in a Phase II FSHD trial — a rare-disease data win that validates a major acquisition and supports the ongoing Phase III. The stock is above both SMAs, RSI is not overbought, and positive phase II reactions in rare-disease assets with no approved treatments historically extend across multiple sessions.
outcome_notes: Zero price movement through the scheduled hold — the Phase II del-brax result generated no incremental buying in the Swiss session, suggesting the data was either pre-positioned before entry or the market treated it as already reflected in the $12B Avidity acquisition premium. The multi-session extension pattern assumed by the thesis did not trigger.
risks_observed: Large-cap pharma Phase II catalysts on acquired assets carry 'expected good news' risk — the acquisition price itself signals internal conviction, leaving the public market less surprised by a positive readout. CHF/GBP FX basis meant the full cost of the position fell entirely on carry with no price offset; strategies relying on post-data drift need a minimum move threshold to be economical.

thesis: Breaking news today (June 12) showing Foundayo hitting a new weight-loss milestone in menopause patients is a new indication catalyst that extends Lilly's GLP-1 dominance narrative; the stock is above both SMAs in a confirmed uptrend with RSI still below extreme overbought territory and room for a continuation move.
outcome_notes: Stopped out at -3% with price moving against the thesis immediately after entry, suggesting the Foundayo menopause milestone was either already priced into the US primary session before Frankfurt opened or that the catalyst was viewed as incremental rather than step-change news. The LLY.DE cross-listing's thinner liquidity likely widened the effective entry spread and steepened the drawdown relative to the underlying NYSE move.
risks_observed: Trading a US-primary catalyst exclusively on a Frankfurt cross-listing introduces independent gap and liquidity risk — LLY.DE can move adversely on open simply due to EUR/USD basis and local order book thinness, independent of the actual news impact. At the basket level, all three positions on this date hit their exits (two scheduled, one stop) with negative P&L, pointing to a session where the news-reactive edge was absent across the board — a correlated signal that the catalyst quality or timing assumptions were systematically off.

thesis: Health Care is the sole Bullish-rated macro sector and Novartis delivers a clear intraday catalyst — the FORTITUDE Phase II win for del-brax (FSHD) validates the $12B Avidity acquisition and arrives into a MACD histogram turning positive from a negative baseline, confirming the technical inflection aligns with the fundamental news. Cost gate of +0.60% is comfortably cleared by a predicted +2.2% move.
outcome_notes: The FORTITUDE Phase II readout failed to generate the forecast +2.2% intraday move — price was exactly flat at the scheduled close, suggesting the catalyst was either pre-priced, released in a window where follow-through was absorbed before the session close, or overshadowed by macro cross-currents. The total return was purely negative after costs despite a nominally flat price.
risks_observed: Event-driven clinical-readout entries carry binary gap risk; a flat close here is the benign outcome, but the same structure can gap against position on data that misses market expectations, with no intraday stop capable of protecting it. Running this alongside ALC.SW created a dual-leg Swiss HC concentration — any CHF headwind or sector rotation hit both simultaneously with no internal hedge.

thesis: Financials are Mildly Bullish and the yield curve has steepened to 91bp (from 86.5bp last week), directly expanding NIM for UK insurers like Legal & General; MACD positive above both SMAs with 20d relative strength of +12.25% vs ISF.L confirming the sector rotation is durable rather than a one-day bounce. Stamp-duty cost gate of +1.00% is clearable given the setup quality.
outcome_notes: LGEN.L printed flat versus entry by the scheduled close, leaving the position a net loser purely on stamp duty and execution costs. Yield-curve NIM expansion is a medium-term earnings driver, not an intraday price catalyst, so without a session-specific trigger the stock had no mechanism to clear the 1% cost gate.
risks_observed: The 1% UK stamp-duty gate demands meaningful directional movement just to break even, making this structure unusually brittle on any flat or low-volatility session — the cost structure is mismatched to the catalyst timeline. Including a Mildly Bullish sector name alongside two high-conviction HC positions also diluted the basket's macro-alignment quality without adding diversification benefit, since all three names were in the same broader risk-on/risk-off regime.

thesis: RSI 6.9 is the most extreme genuine oversold reading in today's candidate set, with normal volume (1.08×) confirming real selling exhaustion rather than illiquidity. No fundamental negative news means this is a pure technical snap-back setup — the widest stop accommodates the low price and bid-ask spread on a £1.49 name.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere across the holding period — the £-15 loss is entirely transaction costs on a flat round-trip, meaning the RSI 6.9 exhaustion signal produced no directional follow-through in either direction. On a £1.49 name the bid-ask spread alone consumes most of the expected edge, so a non-event is functionally a full-cost loss.
risks_observed: Low absolute price amplifies percentage cost drag and makes the per-share spread a meaningful hurdle; even 'normal' volume at 1.08× on a small-cap leaves meaningful liquidity risk if the position needed to be exited quickly. The basket today ran two UK-listed names (SAL.L and PHGP.L) simultaneously, doubling exposure to any UK-specific macro or sentiment shock.

thesis: RSI 20.7 on an AIM miner that just announced high-grade drilling results at Motapa (June 10) provides both a technical and fundamental floor; the ongoing selloff is sector/macro-driven rather than company-specific, and the positive news gives the market a reason to reverse over a 2-day window.
outcome_notes: Price reversed sharply from the oversold entry, reaching the midday take-profit target well within the 2-day window. The fundamental catalyst (Motapa drilling results) appears to have provided the floor the thesis anticipated, with macro/sector pressure abating enough to let the positive newsflow reassert — the exit reason confirms the move was clean and not forced.
risks_observed: AIM miners carry thin liquidity and wide spreads; a gap down on any negative sector headline or broader risk-off move could have trapped the position before the catalyst had time to work. The 7%+ gain in a single session also signals the stock was capable of violent moves in either direction — a stop placed too wide below entry would have been costly if the catalyst had been dismissed by the market.

thesis: Yesterday's identical RSI 19.8 / no-news setup at this ticker cleared +2.0% take-profit in a single session, confirming the capitulation read. The pattern repeats today and the French FTT is manageable given the expected return comfortably exceeds the 1.05% cost gate.
outcome_notes: The prior-session analogue did not repeat — price closed flat and the scheduled exit recovered no reversion, leaving the round-trip cost as a pure loss. A single prior-day success at the same ticker is a weak sample for pattern confirmation; the setup may have resolved cleanly yesterday precisely because it was already oversold, making today's re-entry structurally less compelling.
risks_observed: Recency bias from yesterday's identical setup is the clearest risk here — consecutive same-ticker entries after a prior win inflate conviction without new signal. French FTT is a fixed cost applied at entry, so if the thesis fails the fee cannot be recovered; running this alongside two other scheduled-exit trades on the same day concentrates time-gate risk across the basket.

thesis: RSI 24.2 with 1.76× elevated volume on the decline day is the capitulation washout signature — the elevated volume marks sellers exhausting supply rather than ongoing institutional distribution. Price sits ~8% below the 20-day SMA with no news anchor for the move, creating a clean technical reversion opportunity.
outcome_notes: The elevated-volume capitulation read was correct — price moved to the take-profit level intraday and the midday exit captured the full target. The combination of RSI 24.2 and 1.76× volume on the down day cleanly separated seller exhaustion from ongoing distribution in this instance.
risks_observed: Elevated volume is ambiguous at entry: it equally fits early institutional distribution, which would have extended the decline rather than reversed it. The ~8% gap to the 20-day SMA meant that if the take-profit wasn't triggered, the position would have been carried with substantial mark-to-market drawdown before the scheduled exit; the strategy had no intraday stop to limit that scenario.

thesis: UK gilt momentum has decoupled from US real-rate repricing — the BOE rate-cut path remains intact while the Fed is stuck on hold, giving UK gilts an independent bid that the 3x levered ETF (+7.48% 20d) reflects. The leveraged ATR of ~2.6% daily means the 1.00% cost gate is reachable; tight stop at -2.5% limits downside if US yield contagion spills into gilts intraday.
outcome_notes: Price moved cleanly from entry to the midday take-profit level, suggesting the BOE/Fed policy divergence thesis had real intraday traction. The exit at 62.41 via the planned take-profit trigger indicates no adverse price discovery — the ETF tracked gilt momentum without a disruptive US yield spike bleeding through during the session.
risks_observed: With a single-name leveraged gilt ETF as the sole position, any intraday BOE communication shift or UK inflation print revision would have amplified downside through the 3x lever with no offsetting hedge. The midday exit window is a structural vulnerability — liquidity in 3GIL.L can thin materially in the afternoon, and holding past noon would have exposed the position to US session open volatility with no additional stop adjustment.

thesis: EnQuest announced an $833M acquisition of four Malaysian offshore fields from Petronas (June 10-11) that more than doubles company production — this is a transformative catalyst with multi-session institutional positioning flow. RSI 75.7, volume 1.37x, and positive MACD confirm the trend is intact; the Neutral macro view on Energy is overridden by the company-specific re-rating event.
outcome_notes: Price failed to hold above entry and was stopped out, indicating the acquisition news had already been fully absorbed by the prior two sessions of institutional positioning. The 5.00% drawdown to stop suggests no meaningful buying interest emerged on the day — the catalyst was priced in, not a live driver.
risks_observed: Entering a name at RSI 75.7 on a multi-day catalyst run leaves almost no room for normal intraday noise before the stop is threatened; the risk/reward asymmetry was unfavorable given the already-extended technical position. A single-name, news-driven micro-cap in a Neutral macro sector with no sector hedge amplified downside when the narrative stalled.

thesis: 14.67x average volume is the single strongest institutional flow signal in the entire candidate set — extraordinary demand in a German micro-cap that has gained 24% in 5 days. Low round-trip cost (0.30%) means the signal-to-cost ratio is highly favorable; RSI 76 is elevated but not at exhaustion for the scale of the volume event.
outcome_notes: Extreme volume did not produce follow-through — the position stopped out, consistent with a distribution event rather than accumulation. In German micro-caps, a 14x+ volume spike after a 24% five-day run is ambiguous: it can mark the final absorption leg before reversal, and that appears to have been the case here.
risks_observed: Thin order books in micro-cap Frankfurt listings make stop execution quality uncertain — adverse fill on the way down is likely. Chasing a five-day parabolic move with no identifiable catalyst disclosure means the original volume driver is opaque, which removes the ability to judge whether the thesis is invalidated or just delayed.

thesis: 10.14x volume surge with RSI only 55.8 (substantial room before overbought) in what appears to be a short/inverse S&P product — the combination of exceptional institutional flow and non-extended technicals is the cleaner momentum setup than higher-RSI names. Macro alignment is direct: rising real rates, dollar strength, and tech compression all support the underlying short-equity thesis.
outcome_notes: Exited flat on the scheduled trigger with no directional move materialising, suggesting equity indices were range-bound or the product's tracking was too muted on the session to convert macro direction into price action. The volume signal was real but the session produced no follow-through in either direction.
risks_observed: Inverse/leveraged ETPs carry structural decay that erodes value even when the underlying thesis is directionally correct over time — a flat scheduled exit still incurs implicit holding cost. At the basket level, this position provided partial natural hedging against the two long-risk names, but the hedge was too small in notional terms to meaningfully offset the combined stop losses on ENQ.L and MA10.DE.

thesis: Health Care is the top macro-rated sector (Bullish) and Novartis has a fresh same-day stock-specific catalyst — Phase 2b FORTITUDE trial for del-brax met its primary endpoint, a disease-modifying result in a rare neuromuscular disorder acquired via the $12B Avidity deal. RSI 61.7, above both SMAs, relative strength +7.56% vs SPY in 5 days; 2-day hold allows the data follow-through to play out.
outcome_notes: Price drifted up gradually rather than gapping on the data readout, suggesting the FORTITUDE result was treated as confirmatory rather than transformative by the market. The hold ran to the scheduled window without triggering a profit target, indicating the catalyst delivered at low amplitude. Exit was orderly; no adverse reversal.
risks_observed: A binary rare-disease trial readout carries two-sided tail risk — the muted +0.53% move implies partial pre-pricing of a positive result, which compresses upside while leaving full downside intact if the data had missed. CHF denomination adds currency drag for a GBP book that doesn't appear in the thesis. Any concurrent healthcare names in the basket would have amplified sector concentration on a negative surprise.

thesis: Technology (Mildly Bullish macro) semiconductor equipment is the standout sub-sector today as Musk's Terafab address at ASML's event and the SpaceX IPO debut drive AI capex sentiment; BESI as advanced packaging equipment leader benefits directly from this theme with volume ratio 1.17 confirming conviction, +7.45% 5d above both SMAs, no re-entry penalty.
outcome_notes: Price reversed from entry and hit the stop without recovering, suggesting the AI capex sentiment from the Terafab/SpaceX events did not sustain intraday buying pressure in BESI specifically. The stock was already extended (+7.45% over 5 days) at entry, making it vulnerable to a buy-the-news unwind once the event catalyst was priced in. Stop triggered cleanly; no thesis continuation after exit.
risks_observed: Entering an event-driven name already deep into a multi-day run amplified reversal risk — the 5d gain meant most of the move was borrowed from future sessions. A volume ratio of 1.17 is marginal conviction, not a strong institutional accumulation signal, so the thesis rested heavily on a single-day narrative that dissipated. Broader semis equipment correlation meant any sector-wide fade (e.g. ASML itself softening post-event) would drag BESI regardless of stock-specific merit.

thesis: Today's news brief specifically rates Aerospace/Defense Bullish (Boeing $33bn services backlog), and Rheinmetall is the purest European defense expression — MACD histogram inflecting positive from deeply oversold, above SMA20, +8.12% 20d relative strength, and European rearmament spending is a durable structural tailwind rather than a single-session catalyst.
outcome_notes: The stop triggered quickly, meaning the technical setup — MACD inflection and SMA20 support — failed to hold against what appears to have been discrete selling pressure rather than a grind lower.
