thesis: XLV is the clear macro leader (+7.32% 5d) in a demand-scare defensive rotation, and UNH offers the cleanest execution vehicle: above both SMAs, MACD still confirming positive, and tight ATR ($9.91) ensures efficient risk-parity sizing. Q2 penultimate session keeps institutional rebalancing flows into defensives active for one more day before potential Q3 reversal risk.
outcome_notes: UNH drifted lower throughout the session and the scheduled exit captured the full move without any intraday stop to cushion it. Despite XLV holding macro leadership at the sector level, UNH showed individual mean-reversion pressure — likely exacerbated by managed-care-specific selling or Q2-close rebalancing rotating out of the higher-multiple names within the defensive basket. The technical setup (SMAs, MACD) did not generate follow-through buying interest on the day.
risks_observed: The absence of a trailing stop or intraday exit signal meant the entire intraday drift converted directly into realized loss — scheduled-only exits remove any ability to cut early when a name diverges from its sector. Running UNH and MRK simultaneously in the same XLV basket concentrates both notional and factor exposure; UNH's idiosyncratic underperformance on a day MRK gained 2%+ signals single-name dispersion risk that sector-level macro alignment cannot hedge.

thesis: Merck is the highest-momentum XLV expression (+12.99% 5d) with MACD histogram accelerating and RSI 69.6 not yet at terminal overbought; the CDC Ebola Level-1 activation announcement adds an incremental pharma sentiment catalyst on top of the macro-aligned defensive rotation that has been the dominant regime signal this week.
outcome_notes: MRK continued its momentum leg cleanly into the session and the scheduled exit captured gains near the high end of the day's range. The Ebola catalyst appears to have added a distinct bid on top of the defensive rotation, consistent with the thesis stack — the MACD acceleration entry signal held and there was no intraday reversal to test the conviction.
risks_observed: Entry RSI of 69.6 left limited room before overbought exhaustion risk; a stronger gap-up open would have compressed the remaining upside and increased reversal exposure on a scheduled hold-to-close structure. The Ebola catalyst is headline-driven and binary — any walk-back or competing news could have unwound the incremental bid rapidly with no stop to limit downside, effectively creating asymmetric event risk on the short side that was not sized for separately from the macro trend exposure.

thesis: RSI 20.9 with price 3.5 ATRs below the 20-day SMA and zero news in the 3-day window — this is a pure technical dislocation, not a falling-knife situation. At this depth of oversold (below RSI 21), even a modest mean-reversion bounce well exceeds the 0.90% cost gate for a 2-day hold.
outcome_notes: No bounce materialized — LDOS drifted further from $101.76 to $100.04 over the 2-day hold and was closed on schedule rather than via stop or profit target, indicating the oversold reading wasn't actually exhausted selling pressure.
risks_observed: Pure technical dislocation with zero news is a double-edged signal: absence of news doesn't rule out quiet institutional distribution, and there was no momentum confirmation (e.g. MACD turn) to corroborate the RSI extreme before entry. Defense/IT-services exposure here is uncorrelated with the other two trades, so no basket concentration risk, but the trade highlights the gap in this strategy's exit logic — no early-bail rule when price keeps making new lows intraday during the hold.

thesis: Health Care (XLV Bullish) is the dominant regime trade this week with the defensive rotation driven by a commodity-collapse demand-scare narrative; LLY is the clearest expression — above both SMAs, RSI 72.6 in trend-continuation mode, +12.35% vs SPY 5d, and IBD SwingTrader buying confirms institutional accumulation. Macro-attention conditioning reinforces the pick: rising DXY (101.36, +2.36% 20d) does not impair a primarily domestic US revenue stream, and falling CPI in a demand-scare context rewards non-cyclical necessity spend over growth re-rating.
outcome_notes: LLY drifted up to the scheduled exit without ever needing a stop or target — the defensive rotation into Health Care held through the session, consistent with the commodity-collapse demand-scare narrative staying intact rather than reversing intraday.
risks_observed: RSI was already 72.6 at entry, so the position carried real extension/pullback risk that simply didn't trigger; the trade was also a single-name expression of one sector/macro narrative (XLV bullish, defensive rotation), so any reversal in the commodity-collapse story or a snap-back in risk appetite would have hit this position with no other basket exposure offsetting it.

thesis: RKLB qualifies as a mean-reversion candidate (-21.17% 5d, below SMA20/SMA50) in an XLI (Neutral) aerospace sector; the Iridium acquisition announcement (+11% premarket) is the idiosyncratic catalyst driving reversion, transforming the company from a launch provider into a satellite services platform and re-rating its fundamental value. Risk-off regime constrains this to a single position with a wider stop (-6%) appropriate for elevated volatility.
outcome_notes: Price advanced cleanly from entry through the midday take-profit level, suggesting the acquisition catalyst carried sustained buying rather than a fade after the initial gap. The reversion thesis was validated — the Iridium announcement reset the narrative before the open, and the stock held its gains without requiring the full -6% stop buffer.
risks_observed: Entering after an 11% premarket gap meant absorbing the risk of a classic buy-the-news reversal; a weak broader tape could have pulled the acquisition premium back to entry or worse before midday. The single-position constraint eliminated diversification entirely, so any execution stumble on the Iridium deal (financing concerns, regulatory chatter) would have had full P&L impact with no offsetting legs.

thesis: Primary-grade disclosure anchor: Material Definitive Agreement 8-K filed June 24 (CEPA commercial agreement + warrant issuance to 'Fit') combined with US Export-Import Bank $49M financing approval for South Korean export project — government-backed financing de-risks the international revenue path and the CEPA agreement provides committed off-take structure. As of Friday June 26 close ($24.00), the market had not yet fully reacted (5-day return near flat despite Friday news coverage), and Monday's opening surge confirms institutional absorption is still underway. Stock is above both 20-day and 50-day SMAs with positive MACD and 2.2x average volume. Transitional macro regime (mixed risk-off tone) noted; allocation sized accordingly. No nearby earnings risk (next Sept 9). Stop at -8% exits if the gap-up fades on no institutional follow-through; take-profit at +9% captures the continuation pop without overstaying a single-session catalyst.
outcome_notes: The Monday gap-up (entry ~23% above Friday's $24.00 close) failed to hold, with price fading from $29.47 back through the stop at $27.02 intraday — exactly the scenario the -8% stop was designed to catch. The 'institutional absorption still underway' read was wrong: Monday's open attracted distribution rather than continued accumulation, and there was no follow-through buying to confirm the thesis.
risks_observed: Entering into an already-extended gap amplified the per-share drawdown risk; the stop's percentage trigger translated to a larger absolute move than it would at a pre-gap price. The 8-K's warrant issuance to 'Fit' was a dilution signal embedded in the same catalyst — a likely magnet for short-sellers on a gap-up open. Small-cap fuel cell names in a mixed risk-off macro environment carry elevated reversal risk on single-session catalyst plays, and no intraday confirmation of sustained volume was required before entry.

thesis: EU granted Enhertu its sixth indication via tumour-agnostic HER2-positive approval, substantially widening the drug's commercial footprint beyond any single tumour type; the same session also saw a positive CHMP opinion on Datroway for first-line TNBC, creating dual regulatory momentum that the market has not yet fully absorbed (RSI 63, volume 0.43x average, stock still below the +2% enhanced cost-gate bar that the trail-out penalty requires).
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere from entry — the dual regulatory catalyst (Enhertu tumour-agnostic approval + Datroway CHMP opinion) failed to generate any net price movement by the scheduled exit, suggesting the market had either pre-priced the news or was waiting for clearer commercial guidance before re-rating. The scheduled exit rather than a trail or stop tells the whole story: momentum never developed, so no dynamic exit mechanism had anything to work with.
risks_observed: Low volume (0.43x average) at entry was a visible warning that conviction behind the catalyst was thin — the strategy entered anyway, which is the key failure mode to revisit in the signal filter. With RSI already at 63 and the enhanced cost-gate uncleared, there was upside friction baked in before the position even opened; any adverse drift would have had no trail protection to limit it.

thesis: RSI 19.9 with below-average selling volume (0.42×) points to distribution exhaustion after a -21.35% 20-day selloff; the margin cut and workforce news are operational headwinds already well-priced, not existential, and the cost gate of 0.45%/day is easily cleared by a technical bounce.
outcome_notes: Price kept falling into the scheduled exit rather than bouncing — the 'distribution exhaustion' read on RSI 19.9 and light volume was premature, and the margin-cut/workforce headlines carried more follow-through selling than the thesis assumed. No intraday reversal ever showed up to trigger a take-profit, so the trade rode the drift down to the time-based exit.
risks_observed: Auto-sector, EU-industrial exposure with active negative catalysts (margin cut, layoffs) is a case where 'oversold' can keep grinding lower rather than snapping back — low-volume RSI extremes on names with live fundamental news deserve a tighter leash or smaller size. Also flags basket-level correlation risk if other German autos/industrials were held the same day.

thesis: RSI 8.3 is an extreme oversold reading with no visible fundamental driver behind the slow-grind -7.51% 20-day decline; a technical bounce of >0.75% clears the cost gate, and the asymmetric RSI signal warrants a small position.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere over the holding period and exited flat at scheduled close, absorbing the full spread cost. The RSI-8.3 signal failed to produce any technical bounce, suggesting the slow-grind decline had persistent selling pressure that pure momentum exhaustion could not overcome.
risks_observed: A zero-move on an RSI-8.3 reading is a warning that mean-reversion signals on low-priced, thinly-traded UK small-caps can stall indefinitely — the cost gate is proportionally large at this price level and leaves little margin for a sluggish bounce. No stop-loss on the scheduled exit meant capital was locked in a dead position for the full window with no circuit-breaker.

thesis: Consumer Staples is mildly bullish in the current demand-scare deflation regime and Nestlé is the clearest expression — +6.39% 5d with RSI 69.2, above both SMAs, accelerating MACD, and no negative news headwinds. Predicted +1.2% comfortably clears the 0.60% cost gate.
outcome_notes: Price reversed from entry and hit the stop without recovering, indicating the momentum read was either already exhausted or met near-term selling pressure that the regime signal didn't anticipate. Entering at RSI 69.2 left minimal buffer before the signal invalidated — the 5-day rally was likely priced in at open. Clean directional failure; the stop functioned as intended.
risks_observed: RSI near overbought at entry is a latent exhaustion risk that the scoring underweighted relative to the trend confirmation signals. Consumer Staples momentum plays in a crowded deflation-hedge rotation are prone to intraday profit-taking, and the cost gate of 0.60% provided thin runway once the move stalled. No correlated hedge on the book to offset a sector-wide fade.

thesis: Health Care is the week's dominant bullish sector, and today's EU Enhertu approval for HER2-positive solid tumors (6th indication, tumor-agnostic) is a genuinely fresh catalyst that was absent in yesterday's flat session. RSI 63.4 has room, technicals are clean above SMA20 and SMA50, and predicted +1.8% clears the elevated 1.50% re-entry cost gate.
outcome_notes: The Enhertu approval produced zero price movement on the day, implying the market had fully discounted the sixth indication or that broader sector flows dominated the stock. Scheduled exit recovered entry price but the full round-trip cost was absorbed with no directional contribution — a catalyst trade that behaved like a flat carry position.
risks_observed: A tumor-agnostic label expansion of this breadth is a known watch-list event for institutional desks, making a sell-the-news dynamic or pre-positioning by smarter money a plausible explanation for the non-reaction. The 1.50% cost gate was a yellow flag the model cleared but the underlying liquidity or flow context may not have supported it; holding both a stopped loss (NESN.SW) and a cost-only drag on the same session concentrates the day's P&L damage despite the macro sector call being directionally correct.

thesis: Healthcare is the macro's top-rated sector (XLV +7.12% 5d), and Bayer's Supreme Court Roundup victory removes a decades-long liability overhang that fundamentally re-rates the stock; the DXY strength is a mild headwind on a German name but the stock-level catalyst is dominant — strong MACD, both SMAs below price, and +21% 5d momentum confirm the move is real.
outcome_notes: Price returned exactly to entry by the scheduled close — the Roundup-victory catalyst produced zero net price movement on the day, suggesting it was either already absorbed in prior sessions or failed to attract fresh institutional buying. The £-6.88 loss is pure transaction cost with no price contribution. The 'dominant catalyst' framing wasn't validated by the tape.
risks_observed: Entering a EUR-denominated name on a thesis that explicitly acknowledged DXY as a headwind, then relying entirely on a legal event that predated the trade by at least a session, concentrates single-event timing risk. There was no intraday trigger or volume confirmation to distinguish 'already priced' from 'about to reprice'; that distinction is currently missing from the entry checklist.

thesis: Enhertu's EU tumor-agnostic approval for HER2+ solid tumors (sixth EU indication) is a fresh regulatory milestone that wasn't yet priced on June 29's flat close; XLV healthcare remains the macro's strongest sector and AZN's RSI at 63 with both SMAs below price gives room to run — sized smaller to respect the trail-out cost penalty requiring >1.50% return.
outcome_notes: Flat from entry to scheduled exit — Enhertu's EU approval did not generate measurable intraday price action, consistent with a market that had already discounted the label expansion or was waiting for a US catalyst to confirm. Holding to close netted only cost drag. The >1.50% return hurdle flagged at entry was never approached.
risks_observed: Running AZN alongside BAYN on the same healthcare macro theme on the same day created unacknowledged sector concentration: both positions needed XLV sentiment to hold and both needed an event catalyst to fire within a single session. When neither moved, the correlation between the two losses was near-perfect — the basket acted as a single concentrated healthcare bet, not two independent ideas.

thesis: Reckitt's OTC health portfolio (Nurofen, Dettol, Durex) aligns with today's mildly bullish pharma/consumer-health news tone and the macro's defensive rotation — MACD histogram positive (+0.477), RSI 67 with clean uptrend above both SMAs, no negative stock-specific news, and no trail-out penalty to overcome.
outcome_notes: The stop was hit at -4.50% despite a clean technical picture at entry — RSI 67 and a positive MACD histogram did not prevent a sharp intraday reversal. No stock-specific news was flagged pre-trade, so the move likely reflects either broader consumer-staples/defensives selling or a development that the pre-trade scan missed; either way the technical setup offered no protective lead time.
risks_observed: An RSI of 67 with price already above both SMAs means the stock was entering from an extended position — a mean-reversion move of this magnitude was well within normal range and should have been weighted more heavily against the thesis. With three healthcare/consumer-health longs running simultaneously, a risk-off session or sector rotation hit the entire book at once; no offsetting exposure existed to cushion the stop-out.

thesis: Utilities is the second-strongest macro sector (XLU bullish, +2.91% 5d) and Iberdrola is the cleanest technical expression: RSI 82 in momentum, above both SMAs, MACD positive. The BP/Iberdrola green hydrogen EU approval for Castellón provides a stock-specific catalyst on top of the sector rotation tailwind, with only a 0.30% round-trip cost floor to clear.
outcome_notes: The position closed at the scheduled exit with no price movement captured — entry and exit were flat, so the realized loss is pure transaction cost. Neither the XLU sector tailwind nor the EU hydrogen catalyst at Castellón produced intraday buying pressure, suggesting the approval was already priced in by the open. An RSI of 82 at entry left little upside buffer before the cost floor consumed any marginal gain.
risks_observed: Entering a momentum name at RSI 82 is structurally disadvantaged: the overextension reduces the probability of continuation and shortens the window before mean-reversion pressure kicks in. The strategy has no mid-session stop, so a flat day is structurally a guaranteed loser once transaction costs are accounted for — the 0.30% round-trip floor requires actual movement, not just directional accuracy.

thesis: Health Care is the dominant macro sector (XLV +7.12% 5d, bullish) and AZN's Enhertu just received its sixth EU indication — a tumor-agnostic HER2+ solid tumor approval — which is a different and fresher catalyst than yesterday's failed setup; RSI 63 and both SMAs beneath price leave technical room for continuation despite the re-entry cost penalty.
outcome_notes: Closed flat at the scheduled exit with zero price appreciation; the realized loss is entirely transaction drag. The Enhertu tumor-agnostic approval, despite being characterised as a fresher catalyst, produced no intraday follow-through — consistent with a news event that was already absorbed in prior sessions or in pre-market pricing. The re-entry framing in the thesis was a signal that the catalyst's marginal informational value was already diminishing.
risks_observed: Re-entering a catalyst-driven name after a prior failed setup is a meaningful adverse selection red flag: if the first session failed to move, the odds of the same news driving the second session are compressed. The larger absolute cost loss relative to IBE.MC implies a heavier position in AZN, concentrating Health Care exposure in a single re-entry name the same day — if the sector had reversed, the downside would have been asymmetric to the upside that was actually available.

thesis: ESIH.L is the freshest healthcare entry in the candidate set — RSI 66.6 gives the most upside headroom among leading defensive names while the 2.19× average volume signals new institutional accumulation, not a late chase. With IHCU.L and WHCA.L exiting today, this continues concentrated exposure to the macro-dominant sector (XLV Bullish, +7.12% 5d) through the session's cleanest technical setup.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere — zero return — yet the position lost meaningfully in GBP, meaning the full cost was pure spread and/or currency friction with no offsetting move. The elevated volume signal that underpinned the entry (2.19× avg) did not translate into directional price action, suggesting absorption or distribution rather than accumulation.
risks_observed: High volume without price follow-through is a warning sign the strategy currently treats as bullish; this trade is a clean example of that signal misfiring. Entering a third consecutive healthcare name on the same day the prior two closed created a situation where all three positions shared exit-day correlation, compounding any sector-level adverse move and leaving no uncorrelated leg in the book.

thesis: UKRE.L is the only available candidate sitting in the median sector cluster (Real Estate, rank 4 of 11) while the top-2 sectors (Healthcare, Utilities) must be avoided per strategy rules. Falling 10Y yields (4.37%, declining) are the direct rate-sensitive tailwind for UK REITs, and Q2-close institutional rebalancing into defensive/income positions provides an additional session-specific bid. Predicted +1.8% clears the 1-day 1.25% cost gate; -3%/+4.5% bracket covers ~1.9 ATR on the downside and ~2.8 ATR on the upside.
outcome_notes: Price went nowhere — entry and exit matched exactly, with the £-16 loss coming entirely from transaction costs. Neither the yield-decline tailwind nor the Q2 rebalancing bid produced intraday price movement within the session window; the scheduled exit captured nothing.
risks_observed: Single-name concentration with no fallback: the strategy had only one eligible median-cluster candidate, so a non-event on this ticker meant the whole day's deployment was deadweight cost. The rate-sensitivity thesis operates on a multi-day or multi-week time horizon, making a 1-day scheduled exit structurally unlikely to capture the move even when the thesis is correct.

thesis: ASML's formal denial (June 28) of EUV chipmaking tool sales to China clears the regulatory overhang introduced by the original June 19 Reuters report, which likely drove the 4.1% 5-day pullback within an intact +13.9% 20-day uptrend; the 'new OPEC' framing for chip equipment and the market brief's bullish semiconductor call (AI infrastructure constraint as competitive moat) support a snapback today. Regime: transitional risk-off (VIX estimated 18–28), position sized at moderate conviction accordingly.
outcome_notes: The regulatory-clearing catalyst held: price recovered almost exactly the drawdown caused by the original Reuters report, confirming the overhang was the dominant suppressor rather than any fundamental deterioration. The scheduled exit captured the bulk of the snapback cleanly, though the position closed before it was clear whether momentum would extend further into the 20-day uptrend. No adverse re-escalation of the China EUV narrative emerged intraday to challenge the thesis.
risks_observed: A scheduled exit rather than a signal-driven one means the strategy gave up optionality on continuation — if geopolitical noise had flared again mid-session, there was no dynamic stop to protect against a reversal before the fixed close. EUR/GBP FX drag was a live risk throughout given the euro-denominated listing and sterling P&L. Single-name concentration in a high-profile semiconductor equipment name during a transitional risk-off regime also meant any broader tech sell-off or surprise policy statement from Washington or Beijing could have swamped the stock-specific catalyst.

thesis: Nestlé sits in the XLP sector capturing the current defensive rotation (freshly upgraded to Mildly Bullish, 5d +2.66%), with CHF safe-haven currency providing additional regime-aligned tailwind; the predicted +1.2% clears the 0.75% cost gate, Q2-end window dressing is expected to sustain defensive flows into the close, and this is the only candidate that combines a macro-bullish sector alignment, no re-entry penalty, and a cost gate achievable without an exceptional daily move.
outcome_notes: Price moved against the position from entry, triggering the stop at $82.79 — the predicted +1.2% move did not materialise. The defensive rotation thesis failed to sustain intraday; either window-dressing flows did not emerge or CHF strength reversed, leaving no catalyst to carry price through the cost gate.
risks_observed: Single-name concentration in a low-liquidity cross-listed Swiss name amplified the cost of being wrong on timing. The entry relied on two correlated assumptions — sector rotation and currency tailwind — collapsing simultaneously if macro risk appetite shifted intraday, which is exactly the scenario where stop-outs cluster. No intraday momentum confirmation before entry would have flagged early that the thesis lacked follow-through.

thesis: Medicare GLP-1 coverage for Wegovy/Zepbound launches Wednesday — today is the final positioning session before the structural demand catalyst activates, with last-minute institutional buying driving the intraday move. The catalyst is date-specific, confirmed, and incremental to prior pricing.
outcome_notes: No last-minute institutional buying materialized; LLY drifted lower into the scheduled exit instead of building a pre-catalyst bid. The 'final positioning session' framing assumed the market hadn't already priced Wednesday's Medicare coverage launch, which looks wrong in hindsight.
risks_observed: Single-name, pre-catalyst positioning on a confirmed/dated event is a crowded trade — if the move was anticipatory buying, it likely front-ran days earlier rather than on the eve of launch. Scheduled (time-based) exit with no favorable drift by end of day is itself a signal the thesis wasn't confirming intraday; worth tightening the decision window on dated-catalyst entries rather than holding to the schedule.

thesis: First full trading session as standalone HON Technologies following yesterday's aerospace spin-off completion; Morgan Stanley raises PT to $490 vs $230 current price as analysts begin re-rating the pure-play industrial automation business free of the conglomerate discount.
outcome_notes: Stock fell straight through the session instead of re-rating toward the $490 target, closing down over 4% — the PT raise thesis didn't hold. First-day spin-off dynamics (index-fund forced selling, portfolio rebalancing, profit-taking on the pop) likely dominated any analyst-driven re-rating narrative.
risks_observed: A single outsized analyst PT (roughly 2x the current price) is a weak near-term catalyst and should have been a flag rather than a confirmation signal; spin-off day-one/day-two technical selling pressure is a known, predictable risk that wasn't accounted for in the entry. Basket-wise, this was one of two large-cap names traded today and both landed negative-to-flat, offering no diversification cushion.

thesis: Cantor Fitzgerald raises PT to $850 (+21.8% upside) with stock already +3% premarket, extending yesterday's +11% semiconductor re-rating; AI infrastructure grid-constraint moat narrative is gaining analyst consensus and the reaction is still in its second day.
outcome_notes: Momentum continuation held — AMAT extended the prior day's re-rating on the Cantor PT raise and hit take-profit cleanly, confirming the 'still second day of reaction' read was correct.
risks_observed: Day-2 momentum entries carry reversal risk if the move is already extended on thin follow-through; here it wasn't, but sizing should account for that tail. Sector concentration risk: a semiconductor/AI-infra long sits alongside other basket exposure to AI-adjacent and tech-beta names, so a broad semis pullback would have hit this position independent of the stock-specific thesis.

thesis: AeroVironment's blowout quarterly results today catalysed 'drone super-cycle' coverage that directly reads through to KTOS as a peer defense-drone name, creating a sector-event catalyst on an already oversold RSI-31.6 setup in a broadly bullish defense macro environment.
outcome_notes: The AVAV-to-KTOS read-through didn't hold — KTOS faded through the session despite the 'drone super-cycle' narrative and an oversold RSI-31.6 setup, and the trade exited on schedule rather than via stop or target.
risks_observed: Peer read-through theses are weak when the catalyst is a single competitor's earnings beat rather than KTOS-specific news; oversold RSI alone is not a reliable reversal trigger and shouldn't be treated as confirming evidence. Defense-sector correlation risk is worth flagging at the basket level — a sector-wide 'bullish macro' framing didn't prevent the single largest defense-thematic name in the basket from losing money.

thesis: RSI 21.0 with price 3.7 ATRs below the 20-day SMA and zero news in the window — CME Group's exchange business is unchanged, making this a pure liquidity-driven dislocation. Two-day window gives the bounce time to develop without excessive cost drag.
outcome_notes: Price closed the gap fast enough to trigger the midday take-profit well inside the two-day window, confirming the liquidity-dislocation read — there was no fresh news to explain the bounce, just mean reversion back toward the SMA20.
risks_observed: CME and ICE were both held simultaneously as oversold exchange-operator names; had the sector-wide dislocation been driven by a shared factor (e.g. a rates move or clearing-volume shock) rather than idiosyncratic noise, both legs would have moved together and amplified the drawdown instead of diversifying it.

thesis: RSI 21.4, Goldman Sachs maintains Buy with a $180 target against a $122 close — the analyst community sees no fundamental impairment, making the 17% 20-day selloff a technical overshoot. New futures product launch provides a mild positive catalyst.
outcome_notes: Bounced to the midday take-profit on schedule, with the GS price target and futures-launch catalyst likely helping sentiment turn faster than a pure technical reversion would have on its own.
risks_observed: Same exchange-sector concentration as CME in this basket — the strategy took two correlated bets on the same dislocation theme; reliance on a single analyst's target as the fundamental anchor is also a soft signal that wouldn't have held up if GS revised its view mid-trade.

thesis: RSI 31.3 with MACD histogram flipping positive (+0.36) signals early exhaustion of selling pressure with no fundamental negative news — a short 1-day hold keeps cost drag minimal while capturing the initial bounce.
outcome_notes: Bounce came quickly and cleanly, hitting take-profit within the 1-day window — the MACD histogram flip was a useful leading confirmation on top of RSI that LDOS's setup lacked.
risks_observed: Single-day hold limited exposure but also means the sample size on this exit is thin; a delayed bounce would have forced a scheduled exit at a worse price like LDOS. No fundamental catalyst was identified beyond the technical flip, so this remains a momentum-confirmation bet rather than a thesis with a known floor.

thesis: Dorian LPG dropped 11.88% in 5 days with no news and RSI at 31 — a shipping operator whose Iran exposure is indirect (lower geopolitical risk could open more routes), making it less vulnerable than E&P names to today's Doha oil headwind.
outcome_notes: Price recovered toward the take-profit level despite the Doha oil headline overhang, validating the call that LPG's indirect Iran exposure (shipping routes vs. direct E&P risk) insulated it from the broader energy-sector drawdown that day.
risks_observed: The entry leaned on a discretionary geopolitical judgment rather than a pure technical signal — if Doha headlines had escalated or spread to broader shipping-route risk, the 'indirect exposure' thesis could have failed fast and correlated with other energy names in the basket. Worth flagging that this trade type (geopolitical-overlay reasoning) carries higher tail risk than the RSI-only setups and should be sized or monitored accordingly going forward.

thesis: XLF Neutral sector with a rare triple same-day catalyst: IRS clears Trump Accounts gift-tax reporting today, Robinhood launches the app ahead of the July 4 rollout, and SpaceX is reportedly considering stock donations into accounts — three catalysts compressing into a single pre-holiday event. HOOD is technically sound (above both SMAs, RSI 59.9) and the 2-day hold captures the pre-launch premium before the catalyst fully prices in.
outcome_notes: Price ran from $102.36 to $109.05 well before the holiday close, tripping the midday take-profit rather than needing the full 2-day hold — the pre-launch premium priced in fast, suggesting the market front-ran the July 4 rollout news rather than waiting for confirmation. The triple-catalyst framing held directionally, but the move looks driven more by general fintech/momentum flow than by any single confirmed catalyst (IRS clearance and the SpaceX donation angle were both still speculative at entry).
risks_observed: Thesis rested on three soft/unconfirmed catalysts stacked together — if any one had been denied or delayed intraday, the combined narrative could have unwound sharply given how much of the move happened pre-confirmation. Single-name concentration in a high-beta, sentiment-driven fintech name with no sector hedge; a broader risk-off tape into the holiday would have hit this position hard with no offsetting basket exposure.

thesis: LRCX is the most technically resilient tech candidate — RSI 63.6, well above both SMAs, 20d RS +31% vs SPY — and held +0.40% this week while XLK fell -3.51%, with AMAT +3% premarket today confirming WFE equipment demand is currently isolated from the growth-scare sector rotation; sized at reduced conviction per macro-attention variant rules given XLK remains the Bearish macro call.
outcome_notes: LRCX moved fast enough to clear the midday take-profit, confirming the AMAT-led WFE-equipment strength was a real, isolated pocket of demand rather than noise — the name decoupled from XLK weakness as the thesis expected.
risks_observed: This was effectively a contrarian long against the day's own Bearish XLK macro call, so a broader tech leg-down before the target hit could have erased the gain quickly; reduced conviction sizing correctly priced that conflict, but paired against the LLY/XLV defensive long it also means the basket was running a barbell of opposing sector bets that would both compress in a sharp, indiscriminate risk-off move.

thesis: XLV Health Care is the macro-view's highest-conviction Bullish sector, and LLY benefits from a specific near-term catalyst: Medicare GLP-1 coverage launches Wednesday, pulling forward demand-side positioning alongside the ongoing defensive rotation. The stop at -3% sits just inside 1 ATR ($37.85 / $1229 = 3.08%), limiting loss to one standard move while targeting the expected intraday drift toward the catalyst.
outcome_notes: LLY drifted down through the session and was closed at the scheduled exit rather than stopped out, landing well inside the -3% stop band — the GLP-1/Medicare catalyst thesis was forward-looking to Wednesday, so the position never got to see the event it was actually priced for. Price action looks like generic profit-taking/consolidation after the prior run-up (RSI 74.5 at entry) rather than any thesis invalidation.
risks_observed: Entering on a catalyst that lands after the holding window closes is a timing mismatch — the edge the thesis described wasn't testable in this trade's lifetime. Paired with JNJ in the same XLV sleeve, both legs were correlated defensive-rotation/GLP-1-adjacent bets that moved together on the downside, so the basket carried more single-sector concentration than the per-trade sizing suggests.

thesis: Diversifies the XLV allocation into a large-cap defensive compounder with +11.42% 5d momentum, above both SMAs, and no name-specific headwinds — offering pure sector beta to the confirmed defensive rotation at a slightly lower RSI (73.6 vs LLY's 74.5). The -2.5% stop sits just beyond 1 ATR ($5.52 / $257.70 = 2.14%) to avoid being stopped by normal intraday noise.
outcome_notes: JNJ pulled back modestly and hit the scheduled exit, not the -2.5% stop; the +11.42% 5d momentum/above-SMA setup didn't extend intraday, consistent with a stretched, overbought name (RSI 73.6) cooling off rather than continuing its run.
risks_observed: Both LLY and JNJ entries were already at elevated RSI (>73) before entry, i.e. momentum was chased late in its move — a hindsight signal worth flagging for next time the strategy stacks two near-overbought names in one sector. Combined with LLY, this gave the basket double exposure to the same XLV defensive-rotation factor with no offsetting position, so a sector-wide health-care pullback (which is what today looks like) hits both legs simultaneously.

thesis: The Iridium $8B acquisition catalyst is entering its first full trading session following after-hours momentum, with defense/aerospace explicitly bullish in today's macro brief — the institutional attention from this transformative deal has not been fully absorbed in a single midday session. XLI (Neutral macro rating) is the correct sector alignment; mixed cross-asset regime (one position maximum) justifies modest 20% sizing.
outcome_notes: RKLB ran from $97.85 to the $102.16 take-profit within the midday session, confirming the thesis that the Iridium deal reaction hadn't fully played out — the move looks like continued absorption of the after-hours catalyst rather than a fade. Hitting a midday TP rather than running into the close suggests the bulk of the re-rating was front-loaded early, with momentum cooling by midday.
risks_observed: Sizing was capped at 20% given the mixed cross-asset regime's one-position rule, so this was effectively the entire book's risk for the session — no diversification cushion if the M&A catalyst had reversed (deal-break risk, regulatory friction, or a sell-the-news fade). Single-name, single-sector (aerospace/defense) concentration with no offsetting or correlated hedge position in the basket today.

thesis: Primary anchor: Q3 FY2026 earnings 8-K filed June 24 (+21.2% surprise, within 10-day window) with post-earnings drift thesis still active as analyst consensus of ~$1,542 is 35% above current price. Fresh catalyst today: $250M Trump Accounts investment announcement adds incremental news flow while the -6% 5-day pullback from the post-earnings peak provides a better entry than the initial gap — not a reason to step away, but a reset to re-enter the same disclosure-anchored thesis. Transitional VIX regime applied; sizing reflects 30% reduction from base.

RSI 20.9 with price roughly 4 ATRs below its 20-day SMA and no identifiable negative news — a technical, capitulation-style selloff (volume 1.23x average) in a stable large-cap telecom, favoring a short-term bounce.
outcome_notes: Bounce materialized quickly and cleanly — the capitulation read on a stable telecom with no negative news played out almost exactly as scripted, and the midday take-profit captured the reversion before it could fade.
risks_observed: Fast, clean win on a low-beta defensive name masks that the strategy is relying on volume-driven capitulation reads with no news check beyond 'nothing found' — a quiet fundamental issue could still be missed. No risk materialized here, but the quick exit also means no data on how far the reversion would have run if held longer.

thesis: RSI 24.9 with price ~3.5 ATRs below the 20-day SMA and no company-specific news — oversold energy major likely tracking a broader oil-price move rather than idiosyncratic deterioration, favoring reversion.
outcome_notes: Price essentially round-tripped flat (67.61 to 67.66), so the oversold-energy-major reversion thesis was neither confirmed nor invalidated — TTE just chopped sideways with the broader oil tape rather than snapping back, and the position aged out to the scheduled exit.
risks_observed: A near-zero USD move still booked a small GBP loss, pointing to FX drag between USD-quoted entries/exits and GBP-denominated P&L — worth flagging since it can turn flat trades into small losers independent of the thesis. Also a reminder that macro-driven names (oil majors) can stay range-bound rather than mean-revert on the strategy's timeframe, and correlate with any other energy names in the basket.

thesis: XLV is this week's top-performing sector (+4.26% 5d) and rated Bullish in the macro view; Galderma has the cleanest technical confirmation among healthcare names (above both SMAs, rising MACD histogram, +4.73% 5d rel-strength vs SPY) without being overbought.
outcome_notes: Price drifted in the expected direction but never approached the 4% take-profit or -3% stop before the scheduled close — a modest one-session continuation rather than confirmation of a real breakout, and the move size is within normal noise for a healthcare large-cap.
risks_observed: This leg and NOVN.SW together committed 60% of basket allocation to a single sector (Health Care) and single currency (CHF/XSWX), both sourced from the identical XLV-rotation read — a wrong macro call would have hit both simultaneously with no independent hedge. FX round-trip fees (~£8.41) consumed roughly half the gross gain, a drag that turns comparably-sized future moves into net losses.

thesis: Second expression of the same Health Care rotation thesis — Novartis is trending cleanly (price above SMA20/50, MACD rising) with RSI at a moderate 66.3, offering room to continue without BAYN.DE's exhaustion risk.
outcome_notes: Closed on schedule well short of the 3% take-profit or -2.5% stop, so the 'moderate RSI, room to run' setup was never actually tested — the position simply drifted with typical single-session noise before exit.
risks_observed: Concentration mirrors GALD.SW: same sector, exchange, and macro thesis, so the two positions were not independent bets despite being logged separately. Fee drag was comparable (~£8.41, roughly 40-45% of the gross move), underscoring that on trades this thin, CHF conversion costs are a bigger swing factor in net P&L than the technical signal itself.

thesis: Health Care is this week's confirmed sector leader (XLV +4.26% 5d, #1 of 11) and NOVN.SW offers the cleanest expression: RSI 66.3 (not overbought like BAYN.DE/IBE.MC), MACD histogram still expanding, and my own last trade in this name worked (+1.87%).
outcome_notes: Closed at +0.68%. Follow-through on the previous-day strength held into the close — clean momentum continuation.
risks_observed: Rule-based control has no fundamental or news filter. Today's win is consistent with the strategy's design; watch concentration and sector balance across the basket.

thesis: Healthcare is this week's top-ranked bullish sector in the macro view (defensive rotation confirmed by relative strength), and NOVN is trending cleanly above both SMAs with RSI 66 (not yet overextended) and a rising MACD histogram.

Paired with GALD.SW in the same session, this was the basket's first of two same-sector healthcare longs, concentrating exposure to a single macro call with no offsetting position.

thesis: Second expression of the same healthcare-bullish macro call, with stronger momentum (5d +4.28%, expanding MACD histogram) than NOVN but sized slightly smaller given RSI 68 is closer to overextended.

Combined with NOVN, the basket carried two correlated, same-sector (Swiss healthcare) longs on one macro thesis — a sector-level reversal would have hit both simultaneously with no hedge in place.

thesis: The healthcare/defensive-rotation theme is the strongest macro signal this week (XLV +7.32% 5d, top-ranked sector), and XWHS.L is the only candidate in this basket confirming that move with a genuine 2.84x volume spike rather than a stale carryover setup — RSI 66.6 leaves room before overbought, unlike WHCG.L's 73.7.

The volume spike that distinguished XWHS.L from WHCG.L didn't produce the price action it seemed to signal, suggesting it was more noise than a genuine breakout precursor.
risks_observed: The marginal price gain was fully offset by costs, turning a nominally positive move into a net loss — a reminder that thin, near-flat setups like this carry negative expected value once fees are included. Sizing the trade on a single-name volume confirmation of a sector move is a concentration/idiosyncratic risk: if XWHS.L's spike was unrelated to the broader XLV rotation, the thesis had no real basket-level support to fall back on.

thesis: Two confirmed disclosure-grade events dated today — $1.7B Gulf of America asset sale to Talos/Ridgewood and Rome Export Pipeline regulatory approval — hitting a stock that's still down 9% over 20 days and hasn't re-rated yet, so the reaction looks fresh rather than priced in. Exit was time-based (scheduled), not a stop-out, so the position simply drifted against thesis for the full window without ever inflecting.
risks_observed: This was a counter-trend entry into a name already down 9% over 20 days — trend/momentum risk dominated the news catalyst and wasn't weighted heavily enough at entry. As an energy major, SHELL.AS also carries latent correlation risk to crude price and sector-wide moves that can swamp company-specific disclosures; no evidence the entry checked same-day sector or crude direction as a headwind filter.

thesis: Industrials is the one sector where today's live cross-asset data (XLI +3.97% 5d, +7.44% 20d, ranked #2) contradicts the stale macro note's 'stalled momentum' call and the sector carries no bearish flag; SAF.PA itself is the cleanest expression — genuine uptrend above both SMAs, expanding MACD histogram, +14.4% rel-strength vs benchmark over 20d.
outcome_notes: Thesis held directionally — SAF.PA continued its uptrend from $344.50 to $347.10 — but the move was shallow relative to the setup's framing (sector momentum rank #2, expanding MACD, +14.4% rel-strength). Exit was time-based (scheduled), not a target or stop, so the trade was closed before the trend had a chance to extend or reverse.
risks_observed: Single-name exposure to one industrials name as the sole expression of a sector-wide signal means any SAF.PA-specific news (earnings, guidance, defense-order flow) could have swamped the sector thesis with no diversification to buffer it. The trade explicitly overrode a stale macro note's bearish sector call using live cross-asset data — correct here, but worth flagging as a recurring pattern: if other basket trades also leaned on the same XLI-strength signal, the day's book carries correlated industrials risk that isn't visible trade-by-trade.

thesis: Same-day Micron-GM memory/storage supply agreement plus Apple's CEO flagging an 'extreme shortage' in memory chips are fresh, confirmed catalysts landing today, not stale news — with the stock still only 11% off its 20-day base, the reaction has room to extend rather than being fully priced in.
outcome_notes: Price barely moved despite two same-day catalysts (GM supply deal, Apple's 'extreme shortage' comment) — the news either was already reflected in the pre-entry price or lacked enough surprise to generate follow-through in a heavily-covered mega-cap.
risks_observed: MU is a large, widely-covered name where reactive edge on headline news is inherently thinner than in less-followed tickers; the 'room to extend' framing (only 11% off base) didn't materialize into momentum, suggesting the base-distance heuristic isn't a reliable extension signal on its own. Combined with the HON loss, the basket had zero diversification across the two positions — both large-cap, both news-driven, both underperformed.

thesis: RSI 29.5 with price well below both moving averages, and a fresh positive catalyst (7-year Kuwait Oil Company contract) with zero bearish news — a clean technical oversold setup rather than a falling knife.
outcome_notes: Price never moved from entry and the trade was closed by the scheduled exit rather than a take-profit or stop — the oversold-plus-catalyst thesis simply didn't attract buyers within the holding window despite the Kuwait contract news.
risks_observed: A flat, catalyst-confirmed setup that goes nowhere is a warning sign that RSI/ATR oversold readings alone aren't sufficient without volume or price-action confirmation of reversal; capital sat idle for the full window (opportunity cost) and the position added energy-sector exposure alongside CVX, so the basket had two commodity-linked names with no bounce confirmation in either until CVX's late move.

thesis: RSI 28.1 with capitulation-level volume (2x average) typically marks exhaustion; Morgan Stanley kept its Overweight rating despite trimming the target, so the fundamental view hasn't broken.
outcome_notes: Recovered modestly and hit take-profit, but the move was far more muted than the other winners — capitulation volume plus an unchanged Overweight rating was directionally right but wasn't a strong enough signal to produce a fast reversal.
risks_observed: Paired with SLB as a second energy name, and the two diverged sharply (CVX recovered, SLB went nowhere) — evidence that oversold energy names shouldn't be treated as a uniform basket bet, since single-stock catalysts and volume dynamics dominated over sector-level mean reversion here.

thesis: Most extreme oversold reading in the set (RSI 23.1, 3+ ATRs below SMA20) with no confirming negative news despite the steep decline — sized smaller given the magnitude of the drawdown is unusual for a pure technical dislocation.
outcome_notes: The most extreme oversold reading in the set produced the largest and fastest bounce, hitting midday take-profit well ahead of schedule — validating the idea that deeper dislocations without confirming bad news tend to snap back hardest.
risks_observed: The smaller sizing was the right call given the trade's outlier magnitude — a 3+ ATR dislocation with no visible news catalyst carries real falling-knife risk if there's undisclosed or pending negative information, and CTSH was the only single-name, non-sector-correlated bet in the basket, so it had no offsetting diversification if the thesis had failed.

thesis: Earnings beat (+21.2% surprise, 6/24) is still within the disclosure window and reinforced by today's fresh GM memory/storage supply agreement — a genuine structured catalyst, not just sector sentiment, with the AI-memory-shortage narrative providing corroboration rather than the origin.
outcome_notes: MU drifted essentially flat, closing eight cents below entry with no follow-through on either the earnings-beat or GM supply-agreement catalyst; the position ran out the clock to a scheduled exit rather than hitting a profit target or stop, suggesting the market had already priced in both news items intraday.
risks_observed: Stacking a fresh corroborating headline on top of a nine-day-old earnings surprise didn't generate incremental momentum, a sign the disclosure-window edge decays faster than the thesis assumes; also worth flagging basket-level concentration in AI-memory/semiconductor names, where a shared sector narrative across multiple positions would amplify a reversal even though this single trade's downside was small.

thesis: No pure-play XLV/XLU/XLRE/XLP names are in today's candidate set, but GEV's power-generation/grid-equipment business ties directly into the same falling-yield, heatwave-driven power-demand tailwind that has Utilities and Real Estate rated bullish this week. outcome_notes: Stopped out as the name reversed from RSI 65/expanding MACD into a straight decline, indicating the technical strength at entry was already late-cycle momentum rather than a fresh breakout — the Bernstein initiation bump had likely already been absorbed by the time of entry.
risks_observed: This was flagged at entry as a macro-adjacent proxy standing in for missing XLU/XLRE/XLP pure-plays, and it behaved that way — it carried single-stock risk (large $ price, so a modest % stop is a large dollar loss) without the diversification a true sector basket would give. Using a non-pure-play as a sector stand-in is a recurring pattern worth flagging at the basket level: when the sector candidate set is thin, conviction sizing should probably be capped further, not just labeled 'moderate.'

thesis: Health Care is the macro-bullish, sector-strength-ranking leader (top of today's snapshot, macro brief upgraded XLV to Bullish), and LLY's own technicals (above both SMAs, positive MACD, clean 5d/20d uptrend) confirm the sector call. outcome_notes: LLY tracked through to the take-profit level cleanly, confirming the Health Care sector-strength call — the name traded with its established 5d/20d uptrend intact rather than chopping, suggesting the XLV bullish upgrade was the real driver rather than noise.

Fixed take-profit exit also means no read on whether LLY/XLV strength extended further intraday.

thesis: Corning's addition to the Russell Growth Indexes is a confirmed, fresh catalyst driving 2x average volume into a stock already in a strong uptrend (above both SMAs, bullish MACD) — the reaction is still actively developing, not yet priced in, and it aligns with today's bullish AI-infrastructure capex theme.
outcome_notes: Price ran cleanly from $192.96 to the $202.61 take-profit without needing to test a stop, consistent with the index-inclusion volume thesis actually following through rather than fading intraday. The move looks driven by continued passive/index-tracking flow plus the broader AI-capex tailwind rather than a reversal or news fade, so the catalyst read was correct and timely.
risks_observed: Single-name concentration in a stock already extended above both SMAs meant the trade was chasing momentum late in its move — a less clean tape could have seen the same gap-up reverse into the entry price. No explicit correlation check against other AI-infrastructure-capex names in the basket that day, so if several such trades were open simultaneously the strategy carried undiversified sector/theme exposure even though this individual trade resolved favorably.

thesis: Consumer Staples is the macro view's mildly-bullish, best-confirmed defensive-rotation sector this week (XLP +1.69% 5d, XLV/XLU/XLP leading broadly); Danone's clean uptrend (above SMA20/50, RSI 73, +2.45% rel-strength) is the sharpest un-stopped, un-repeated setup within that theme, clearing the 1.40% FR cost-gate floor with margin.
outcome_notes: Closed near flat at +0.00%. Drifted sideways through the session — no follow-through but no meaningful reversal either.
risks_observed: The rule-based control can't distinguish 'rallying on solid fundamentals' from 'rallying on a squeeze about to unwind.' This loss validates the case for news-aware and mean-reverter strategies that would have filtered it.

thesis: RSI 29.5 with no negative news — same capitulation-into-stable-telecom setup that worked yesterday, now on a fresh leg down to $24.43, a clean re-entry for a bounce toward the 20-day SMA.
outcome_notes: Price reverted quickly enough to trigger the midday take-profit, confirming the capitulation-bounce read for a second consecutive entry in this name. No new catalyst emerged — the move reads as pure mean reversion off an oversold RSI, consistent with yesterday's pattern.
risks_observed: Two back-to-back entries in the same ticker inside two days is a concentration risk if the 'capitulation' read is ever wrong — the strategy doubled down on one telecom name's technical signal rather than diversifying across setups. The stop-loss discipline was never actually tested since the bounce resolved cleanly and fast.

thesis: RSI 25.8 and well below both moving averages, but the recent headlines are sector-wide M&A activity among peers (Eni, Shell, TotalEnergies) with nothing BP-specific negative — looks like indiscriminate energy selling, not a company problem.
outcome_notes: Price never moved off entry — the anticipated indiscriminate-selling bounce didn't materialize intraday, and the position was closed flat on schedule rather than stopped out or taking profit. The 'sector noise, not company-specific' read may have been directionally fine but mistimed for a single-day hold.
risks_observed: BP.L and GLEN.L both closed flat on scheduled exits the same day — two UK commodity/energy names failing to revert together points to a broader risk-off tone in that corner of the basket rather than isolated technical setups, a correlation the per-ticker headline screen wouldn't catch.

thesis: RSI 17.7 is a deep oversold extreme, price detached sharply from its 20/50-day MAs with no confirming negative news in the headlines, setting up for a snapback toward the mean.
outcome_notes: The deep RSI extreme resolved fast, hitting the midday take-profit for the day's best return — a clean snapback with no contradicting news, validating the 'no confirming negative news' filter at this RSI level.
risks_observed: An RSI this extreme (17.7) can just as easily mark the start of a structural breakdown as noise; today's clean bounce shouldn't be read as proof the headline screen reliably tells the two apart. Basket-level, this and DTE.DE gave two DE-listed winners against two flat UK names — a geography/exchange split worth watching for recurrence.

thesis: RSI 30.1 and price below both MAs; the only headline is a departing executive to a rival miner, not a fundamental miss — treating as a technical oversold bounce with a tighter stop given the added uncertainty.
outcome_notes: The tighter stop taken for the executive-departure uncertainty was never needed — price simply sat flat all session and was closed on schedule, so the oversold-bounce thesis didn't play out either way within the holding window.

Both scheduled-exit flats being UK/commodity-sector reinforces a sector-correlation risk the strategy currently isn't screening for.

thesis: Health Care is the only sector this week where the macro view's bullish call is actually confirmed by real price leadership (top of the strength ranking), and Roche's uptrend (above both SMAs, expanding positive MACD histogram) plus FDA priority-review news is a clean stock-level expression of that regime shift into defensives.

outcome_notes: Price was unchanged from entry to exit, so the 'room left to run' RSI/MACD setup never got a chance to play out before the scheduled close closed it out. The loss is entirely transaction cost, not a failed breakout.

Both trades share UK exchange listing and defensive-rotation sector exposure, so a single macro or feed problem could sink the whole basket at once; that concentration isn't visible from the individual trade view.

thesis: ASML raised revenue guidance yesterday citing stronger-than-expected AI infrastructure chip demand — a primary-grade guidance-revision disclosure in a sector the macro brief flags bullish, with price still above both moving averages and RSI not yet overbought, suggesting the reaction is still developing rather than priced in.

Price broke below both moving averages instead of extending the guidance pop, and the position was closed on the scheduled 1-day exit at -1.43%, just short of the -2.5% stop.
risks_observed: Position sized at ~24% allocation on a single-name, single-catalyst entry — no mechanism flagged that a second, negative disclosure (regulatory/export-control) could arrive intraday and dominate the bullish guidance news. ASML/EU semicap equipment carries recurring geopolitical export-control headline risk that this strategy doesn't currently screen for pre-entry, and the name itself was only added to the universe post-hoc after this trade.

thesis: XLV is this week's top-rated bullish sector in both the macro call and confirmed sector-strength data; LLY's uptrend (RSI 62.8, rising MACD, price above both SMAs) is the clean momentum expression of that rotation, not yet overbought like ABBV.
outcome_notes: Price was essentially unchanged from entry to the scheduled exit — the RSI/MACD momentum setup never produced follow-through, and the position was closed flat rather than extending the uptrend.
risks_observed: This was one of three same-day XLV positions (with UNH and JNJ), so it added to concentrated sector exposure without contributing a diversifying return; a scheduled exit with zero price movement suggests the entry lacked a near-term catalyst to actually move the name.

thesis: Second leg of the healthcare defensive-rotation thesis — UNH shows the same bullish-sector alignment with confirmed institutional (whale) accumulation and a technically clean uptrend.
outcome_notes: The thesis broke down outright — price fell ~3% and hit the stop, so the cited whale accumulation and clean uptrend did not hold as support intraday.
risks_observed: As the second leg of a three-name XLV rotation trade, this stop-out crystallized correlated sector risk rather than an isolated miss; there's no sign the whale-accumulation signal was screened against name-specific downside risk that could override the broader sector call.

thesis: Diversifies the XLV rotation trade across a third large-cap healthcare name with a steady uptrend (RSI 65.9, expanding MACD histogram) and no name-specific negative catalyst.
outcome_notes: Price rallied cleanly into a midday take-profit with no adverse news, matching the steady-uptrend/expanding-MACD setup described at entry.
risks_observed: Despite the win, JNJ was still directly correlated with the same-day UNH stop and LLY's flat trade — one sector-level macro read produced three correlated healthcare bets rather than true diversification, so the basket's net risk was larger than any single trade's P&L suggests.

thesis: RSI 27.4 and 1+ ATR below both SMA20/50 with no bad news — the sell-off looks technical, and a same-day Wolfe upgrade to Outperform ($210 PT) confirms the bounce case.
outcome_notes: Price reclaimed ground quickly, closing the gap toward SMA20 within the same session and triggering the midday take-profit before the setup had time to fully mean-revert. Hard to separate the technical bounce from the Wolfe upgrade's own price impact — the two landed on the same day, so this reads more like a catalyst-driven pop than a clean oversold reversion.
risks_observed: Entry thesis leaned on 'no bad news' plus a same-day upgrade as confirmation, which is a look-ahead-adjacent signal — an upgrade landing intraday isn't something the strategy can count on repeating, so the edge here may be overstated for future oversold-CVX setups. Single-name energy exposure with no visible hedge against broader oil/sector moves; worth checking whether other basket positions that day carried correlated energy or macro-rate exposure.

thesis: RSI 25.4 with 2x normal volume and no negative headlines — classic capitulation-then-bounce setup, deepest oversold reading in the clean-news bucket.
outcome_notes: Bounce was immediate and sharp, hitting take-profit same session — the capitulation read on 2x volume was correct and the reversal didn't need overnight confirmation. No follow-through news emerged to explain the move, consistent with a pure oversold snapback rather than a fundamental repricing.
risks_observed: This was the single deepest RSI reading in the bucket, so it carried the most idiosyncratic risk if the volume spike had instead been distribution rather than capitulation — worth flagging since that tail risk simply didn't hit today. No sector overlap with the other two names, so it wasn't a source of basket correlation.

thesis: RSI 32.9, ~2 ATR below SMA20, no confirming bad news — modest oversold drift that should partially revert.
outcome_notes: Reversion was proportionate to the modest RSI/ATR setup — a partial, orderly recovery rather than a violent snapback, matching the entry thesis's own framing of 'partial reversion.' Take-profit triggered midday with no news catalyst, suggesting mean reversion mechanics rather than a fundamental re-rate.
risks_observed: Consumer-staples exposure overlapped with PEP in the same basket on the same day — both oversold, both reverting simultaneously raises the question of whether this was sector/defensive-rotation beta rather than two independent idiosyncratic setups. High per-share price means dollar concentration risk is larger than the position count implies.

thesis: RSI 31.9 on a sharp, recent-only pullback; analyst PT trims are routine, not an earnings-miss or scandal, so the reversion case stays intact.
outcome_notes: Move was much stronger than the moderate RSI reading implied, snapping back to take-profit within the session; the read that PT trims were noise rather than a real negative catalyst held up. Speed of the reversal suggests the pullback was thin/liquidity-driven rather than conviction selling.
risks_observed: Ran concurrently with COST, another consumer-staples name reverting the same day — sector concentration risk in the basket that the individual entry screens (RSI, news check) wouldn't catch, since neither trade's diligence looks at cross-position sector exposure. If today's broad tape was simply risk-on, both fills may be riding a common macro driver rather than stock-specific mean reversion.

thesis: XLV is the week's strongest sector by a wide margin under the demand-scare/defensive-rotation macro regime; LLY is the highest-quality large-cap expression, trading above both SMA20/50 with a rising MACD and RSI (62.8) not yet at exhaustion levels.
outcome_notes: Position went nowhere all session — entry and exit prices were identical — and was closed only because the holding window expired, not because the thesis played out or failed. The XLV-strength/technical-momentum setup never got a chance to express itself; LLY simply chopped in place around 1184 all day.
risks_observed: A flat, non-moving large-cap name still ties up capital and basket slots for a full session with zero information gained — that's an opportunity-cost risk more than a market risk. Worth flagging that the strategy has no mechanism to cut a stalled trade early and redeploy into a live setup; everything rides the scheduled exit regardless of whether price action confirms or denies the entry read.

thesis: Financials is macro-neutral, not a tailwind, so sized smaller than LLY — but today's stock-specific catalyst (Mizuho/BTIG price-target raises, new blockchain/tokenized-stock product) is a genuine idiosyncratic driver on top of an already-confirmed uptrend.
outcome_notes: The idiosyncratic catalyst (analyst target raises, tokenized-stock product news) did not overcome broader pressure on the name — HOOD gave back over 4% and the stop triggered cleanly, meaning the 'confirmed uptrend' broke down intraday rather than extending on the news.
risks_observed: Reduced sizing for a macro-neutral sector didn't prevent a full stop-out, showing that single-stock catalyst trades can still get run over by broader tape/volatility even when the sector call itself was cautious. Also worth checking whether HOOD's move was correlated with other high-beta/momentum names in the basket that day — if several positions leaned on similar risk-on assumptions, the stop here may be an early signal of a basket-wide regime shift rather than a stock-specific miss.

thesis: Regime signal is mixed today (tech partially reversing off the macro view's bearish call, credit only mildly widening) so I'm cutting to one highest-conviction momentum name rather than blending modes. HOOD sits in a Neutral-rated sector (clears the bearish-sector filter), has a clean uptrend not yet overbought (RSI 64.5, above both SMAs), and carries a live catalyst — same-day Mizuho/BTIG price-target raises plus a blockchain/tokenized-equity expansion announcement.
outcome_notes: HOOD reversed intraday and never extended the pre-entry uptrend, tripping the stop about 3% below entry; the price-target raises and tokenized-equity headline didn't produce follow-through buying, suggesting the news was either already priced in or was overwhelmed by broader risk-off flow later in the session.
risks_observed: Concentrating the day's entire allocation in one name on an admittedly mixed-regime day left no offsetting exposure when the single pick failed — a diversified 2-3 name basket would have diluted this stop-out. The 'clears the bearish-sector filter' framing was a soft signal, not a hard edge, and catalyst-driven entries on names already up near RSI 65 carry elevated give-back risk once the news pop fades, which is exactly what played out here.

thesis: Reconciled from Alpaca portfolio (slot 1) — original ledger entry missing (likely an entry-run timeout or smart-merge race). Daily exit will close this normally.
outcome_notes: META was bought into a wave of bullish AI-cloud-strategy news and analyst price-target raises on heavy volume, but the move reversed intraday — the stock closed down for the session and the position exited at the scheduled daily close rather than any early stop, riding the full reversal. The same fade hit other AI-cloud-linked names that day (e.g. CoreWeave -4.81%), suggesting the initial pop was sold off broadly once the news was priced in rather than this being a META-specific failure.
risks_observed: This position had null stop_loss_pct/take_profit_pct and a 0.0 allocation_pct because it never went through the normal entry pipeline — it was reconstructed after the fact from the broker's actual holdings following an entry-run timeout or smart-merge race, meaning it sat with zero downside protection for the entire session. That's a pipeline-reliability risk, not a market risk, and worth flagging separately from the trade thesis; on the basket level, the day's other news-reactive pick (Corning, AI-infrastructure capex theme) shared the same underlying AI-capex narrative, so the strategy carried undiversified thematic exposure to that story fading.

thesis: Confirmed Ukraine artillery contract win plus fresh German government push for domestic Tomahawk/Patriot production with US collaboration — a live, developing defense catalyst with price still below both SMAs, so the reaction isn't fully priced in yet.
outcome_notes: Price continued lower after entry and hit the stop at $1080.58, a straight -3% move with no bounce — the contract-win/Tomahawk headline didn't generate the expected follow-through buying. Being below both SMAs at entry was framed as upside not yet priced in, but it more plausibly reflected existing selling pressure that the news failed to reverse.
risks_observed: Entering below both SMAs on a supposedly bullish catalyst is a trend-fighting setup — treat sub-SMA price action as a warning sign rather than an opportunity unless there's confirming volume/momentum. RHM is the largest, most crowded EU defense name, so any single-name defense trade carries basket-level correlation risk to the same German-rearmament narrative; check whether other defense tickers in the basket also faded on 2026-07-03 before treating this as an idiosyncratic miss.

thesis: Health Care is the macro view's single strongest bullish call and today's top-performing sector (XLV +5.21% 5d) — NOVN.SW is in a confirmed uptrend (above SMA20/50, MACD histogram positive) with a fresh EC gene-therapy approval catalyst, and trading it alone today avoids repeating this week's CHF/XSWX sector-concentration issue from stacking it with GALD.SW.
outcome_notes: Price faded straight through entry to the stop at $125.48 (-2.50%) with no follow-through on the gene-therapy catalyst; the SMA20/50 uptrend and positive MACD histogram that justified entry didn't hold intraday, suggesting the setup was already extended or the catalyst was priced in before entry.
risks_observed: Trading NOVN.SW solo did sidestep the CHF/XSWX stacking issue, but as the day's sole macro-aligned position it left basket P&L fully dependent on one name and one catalyst holding up — a technical-uptrend + news-catalyst combo with no confirmation of intraday momentum before entry, which this stop-out shows isn't sufficient on its own; future entries in this sector should wait for intraday price confirmation rather than acting on 5d sector strength alone.

thesis: Healthcare is the macro view's top bullish call and today's sector snapshot confirms it (XLV +5.21% 5d, the market's clear leader). Roche is technically clean (above both SMAs, positive MACD histogram, RSI 63.7 — not overbought) with a fresh, real catalyst: its KRAS drug beat existing lung-cancer therapies in a late-stage trial.
outcome_notes: Roche drifted lower into the scheduled close despite the clean technical setup — the KRAS trial beat either failed to gain traction intraday or was already reflected in the open, and there was no stop or target to react to the fade.
risks_observed: The sole loser in today's basket, and a reminder that a genuinely fresh catalyst doesn't guarantee same-day follow-through. At the basket level, this was one of two healthcare longs sized off the same sector-strength read, so the miss here still leaves healthcare as half the day's gross exposure with no diversification against a sector-wide read failing.

thesis: Industrials is Neutral (not rejected) in the macro view, and today's news brief explicitly flags Defense as a bullish theme off the UK's $20B military overhaul headline. BAE's technicals confirm — above both SMAs, positive MACD histogram, RSI 62.6 with room to run.
outcome_notes: The technical setup (above both SMAs, positive MACD histogram, RSI 62.6) failed to produce follow-through — price reversed almost immediately and ran straight through the stop, suggesting the defense-headline catalyst was already priced in or met with profit-taking rather than fresh buying. No evidence the $20B overhaul story drove any incremental demand for BAE shares on the day; the stock traded like a stock giving back an extended move, not one reacting to positive news.
risks_observed: RSI 62.6 at entry was already on the elevated side of neutral, meaning the trade was momentum-chasing into a move with less room left than the thesis implied — a classic late-entry risk on a headline-driven setup. Single-name entry on a sector-wide theme (Defense/Industrials) with no apparent diversification check also concentrates the strategy's exposure to one interpretation of a Neutral-rated sector call.

thesis: RSI 10.8 is the most extreme oversold reading in the basket with no confirming bad news, mirroring the DTE.DE/IC2.DE capitulation-bounce setups that paid off this week.
outcome_notes: Price was completely unchanged from entry to the scheduled exit — the most extreme oversold reading in the basket produced no bounce at all, so the capitulation thesis was never actually tested by the market. The loss is pure cost drag, not evidence against the setup.
risks_observed: A dead-flat print on the highest-conviction RSI reading of the day raises a stale-quote/illiquidity concern rather than a clean thesis failure. Combined with the other two names also closing flat, this looks like a basket-wide pattern (possibly a quiet session or data issue) rather than three independent idiosyncratic misses, which is worth checking before trusting today's RSI signals going forward.

thesis: RSI 23.8 and price well below both the 20- and 50-day MAs after a 13.7% pullback, with news flow showing sector strength rather than any TTE-specific negative catalyst.
outcome_notes: No movement whatsoever between entry and the scheduled exit despite the 13.7% pullback and deep oversold reading — the reversion setup simply never got engaged by the market. Loss is attributable entirely to transaction cost on the largest notional of the three, not a failed bounce.
risks_observed: Largest position of the batch sat with zero realized volatility, tying up capital without the thesis ever being tested — a capital-efficiency risk as much as a market one. Also worth flagging sector/geography concentration (European energy large-cap) against any other TTE- or energy-adjacent exposure held in the basket same day.

thesis: RSI 25.2 below both moving averages with no adverse headlines — a modest technical bounce candidate, sized smaller given the weaker oversold reading.
outcome_notes: Flat from entry to scheduled exit, consistent with this being the weakest-conviction setup (RSI 25.2) of the three — but since price never moved at all, the modest-bounce thesis was untested rather than disproved.
risks_observed: The £15 loss looks disproportionate to the stated smaller sizing given the sub-£1 share price, suggesting the size reduction may not have scaled exposure down as intended — worth auditing position-sizing logic for low-priced names. At the basket level, all three oversold candidates today printed flat, a pattern that deserves scrutiny before relying on RSI signals from this session again.

thesis: Defense/Industrials is macro-neutral but today's UK £20B military overhaul headline plus Rheinmetall's parallel defense pop confirm sector tailwinds are real and current; RSI 62.6 with a fresh bullish MACD histogram crossover leaves room to extend the move.
outcome_notes: Stopped out for -3% within the session despite the fresh defense headline and RSI/MACD setup — the pop off the £20B overhaul news and Rheinmetall correlation didn't extend, suggesting the catalyst was already reflected in price by entry and the stock simply mean-reverted.
risks_observed: Entering at RSI 62.6 left little room before overbought exhaustion, and the thesis leaned on a same-day headline plus a correlated peer's move (Rheinmetall) rather than an independent signal — a same-day, sentiment-driven entry with no idiosyncratic confirmation. It was also the first of two stops today, both in nominally 'bullish' sectors, hinting at broader tape weakness rather than sector-specific failure.

thesis: XLV is the macro view's top-rated bullish sector and AZN is trading above both SMAs with strong rising MACD; fresh EU tumor-agnostic Enhertu approval gives a name-specific catalyst on top of the sector tailwind.
outcome_notes: Also stopped out at -2.5% despite the Enhertu approval catalyst and rising MACD — the name-specific news failed to offset broader price pressure, and the stock broke below both SMAs shortly after entry rather than extending the uptrend.
risks_observed: A drug-approval headline is a one-off catalyst with no guarantee of follow-through volume, and relying on 'top-rated bullish sector' status didn't protect against a same-day reversal. Combined with BA.L's stop, two of three trades in unrelated 'bullish' sectors failed the same session — worth checking whether a broader UK/FTSE risk-off move was the actual driver rather than sector mis-tagging.

thesis: Consumer Staples (XLP) was just upgraded to mildly bullish on defensive rotation, and ULVR is cleanly trending above both SMAs with added support from bid-interest speculation.
outcome_notes: Closed flat on a scheduled/time exit rather than hitting stop or target — the defensive-rotation and bid-speculation thesis never produced directional movement intraday, leaving the position to expire at breakeven minus costs.
risks_observed: No stop was triggered because the trade simply went nowhere, but that also means the setup provided no edge — 'bid-interest speculation' is an unconfirmed, rumor-level driver with no price confirmation. Across the basket, all three sector-tag-driven trades underperformed today (two stops, one dead flat), suggesting the macro sector-rating signal itself was unreliable in this session and shouldn't be trusted alone for entries without a firmer technical or news trigger.

thesis: EU approval of Enhertu as first tumor-agnostic HER2-ADC (2026-07-02) is a primary-grade regulatory disclosure expanding the drug's addressable population; volume ratio of only 0.74 shows the market hasn't fully confirmed the move yet, leaving room to run before next earnings on 2026-07-27.
